text: EX-10.7 11 ex10-7.htm EX-10.7 Exhibit 10.7 EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT THIS EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is being made as of November 1, 2026 between Patriot Glass Solutions, LLC, a Texas limited liability company (“PGS” or the “Company”) having its principal offices at 2029 Pat Booker Road, Universal City, TX 78148, and Michael Wanke (the “Employee”) an individual with an address at [*]. NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the mutual premises and agreements contained herein, and intending to be legally bound hereby, the parties hereto agree as follows: 1. Nature of Employment; Term of Employment . PGS hereby employs Employee and Employee agrees to serve PGS as its Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”), upon the terms and conditions contained herein, until three (3) years from the date of this Agreement, unless terminated sooner pursuant to the terms hereof (the “Employment Term”). 2. Duties and Powers as Employee . (a) During the Employment Term, Employee shall be employed by PGS as its CEO and shall have such powers and duties as are delegated and conferred upon him from time to time by the Authorized Manager of PGS. Employee agrees to devote Employee’s full business attention and best efforts to the performance of Employee’s duties and to the furtherance of PGS’s interests, a primary goal of which is to increase revenues and profit. (b) As CEO of PGS, Employee’s responsibilities will include providing leadership and direction to the Board of Managers of PGS (the “Board”), facilitating the operations and deliberations of the Board and satisfying the strategic initiatives of PGS. (c) As CEO of PGS, Employee’s primary responsibilities also include managing the day to day operations and resources of PGS, acting as the main point of communication with the Authorized Manager. (d) As CEO of PGS, Employee will be required, under direction of the Authorized Manager to fully cooperate with the operations of any and all other operating businesses of TLSS Acquisition, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“TA”) and its affiliates, including its parent, Transportation and Logistics Systems, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “Corporation”), to help maximize TA’s and the Corporation’s revenue and profit and acquisition opportunities including but not limited to, sourcing, assessing, and integrating business lines, when applicable, with and into PGS. 1 (e) Employee’s principal place of employment shall be in Universal City, Texas area and during the Employment Term, Employee will not be required to relocate outside of the San Antonio-New Braunfels metropolitan area. Employee may be required periodically to travel in connection with Employee’s duties and for other normal business reasons. 3. Compensation . (a) Base Salary and Bonuses . (i) In consideration of Employee’s services, Employee will be paid an initial base salary of $118,000 in year one (the “Base Salary”) payable in accordance with PGS’s payroll practices. Base Salary for years two and three of the Employment Term will be reviewed annually. (ii) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the parties hereby agree to an interim Base Salary review ninety (90) days after the commencement of this Agreement, during which time, it will be determined by the CEO of the Corporation, as to when it will be the appropriate time to increase Employee’s Base Salary to $170,000 on a going forward basis for the remainder of first year of the Employment Term. (iii) Ninety (90) days after the commencement of this Agreement, with respect to the first year of this Agreement and thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of each subsequent year of the Employment Term, the parties will mutually agree to a bonus program pursuant to which bonuses will be payable upon achieving certain bonus milestones (“Bonus Milestones”). The timing of the payment of such bonuses, provided Bonus Milestones are met, will be mutually agreed upon during such initial ninety (90) day period. (iv) Bonus Milestones shall be based upon PGS achieving certain financial results for EBITDA, on a quarterly basis. For purposes of the bonus calculation, the Operating EBITDA of PGS operations will be based upon the improvement or increase over projected (or budgeted) combined EBITDA results, before any expenses associated any other non-cash expense that is unrelated to the operation of PGS business. (v) For clarification, the Employee’s Base Salary and the bonus program, including the Bonus Milestones, shall be reviewed annually and renegotiated in good faith, at least thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of each year during the Employment Term. (b) Initial Option Grant and Vesting. (i) On the Employee’s start date, subject to the approval of the Board of Directors of the Corporation and/or its Compensation Committee, the Corporation shall grant the Employee an option (the “Option”) to purchase a number of shares of the Corporation’s Common Stock equal to the value of $730,000 based on the fair market value of the Corporation’s Common Stock at the time of the grant. 2 (ii) Subject to the Employee’s continued employment through each applicable vesting date, the Option shall vest and become exercisable over a three (3) year period as follows: One-third (1/3rd) of the shares shall vest on the first anniversary of the Executive’s start date, and the remaining two-thirds (2/3rds) shall vest in equal annual installments over the following two (2) years. (c) In addition, Employee shall have the opportunity to earn an annual discretionary bonus in the form of non-qualified stock options or restricted stock units in the Corporation, whichever is available and as determined by the Board and the Board of Directors of the Corporation. Such discretionary bonus shall be based upon the Authorized Manager’s evaluation and the CEO of the Corporation’s evaluation of certain overall performance criteria, including such as, but not limited to: (i) Employee’s implementation of operating efficiencies; (ii) significant new customer contracts; (iii) the implementation of new business initiatives; and (iv) coordination with other business units. Such discretionary bonus could be valued up to 50% of your Base Salary and any such grant would vest equally over a one-year period following the date of grant. 4. Benefits . Employee will be eligible to participate in any employee benefit plans and programs generally available to the Company’s executives, including health and other benefits, subject to the terms and conditions of such plans and programs, provided however, that the Company shall pay the premiums associated with the Employee’s participation in the Company’s medical and dental plans or reimburse Employee monthly for the Employee’s current insurance plan if Employee does not participate in the Company’s plans. 5. Expenses; Vacations; Personal Days . (a) During the Term hereof, Employee shall be entitled to reimbursement for reasonable travel and other out-of-pocket expenses necessarily incurred in the performance of Employee’s duties hereunder, upon submission and approval of written statements and bills in accordance with the then regular procedures of PGS. (b) During the Employment Term hereof, Employee shall be entitled to paid vacation time in accordance with then regular procedures of PGS governing employees as determined from time to time by PGS’s Board of Managers. At this time, the Employee is entitled to four (4) weeks of vacation per calendar year but at such times, approved in advance by the CEO or CFO of the Corporation, provided that they do not interfere with the management or supervision of the operation. Any unused vacation time (or accrued vacation pay) will be carried over to ensuing calendar years. (c) During the Employment Term hereof, Employee shall be entitled to five (5) personal days each calendar year. Employee shall not be permitted to take more than two (2) consecutive personal days, whether or not such days are in different calendar years. Any unused personal days may not be carried over to ensuing calendar years. 3 6. Representations and Warranties of Employee . Employee represents and warrants to PGS that he is under no contractual or other restriction or obligation which is inconsistent with the execution of this Agreement, the performance of Employee’s duties hereunder, or the other rights of PGS hereunder. 7. Confidentiality; Non-Competition . (a) Except in connection with Employee’s employment with PGS, Employee will not, directly or indirectly, use for himself or disclose to any other person or entity any confidential information concerning PGS for any purpose whatsoever, without the prior written consent of the Board of Managers of PGS. For purposes of this Agreement, “confidential information” shall not include information that: is or becomes a part of the public domain (other than by a breach of this Agreement), is or was rightfully received by Employee from a third party not obligated to hold such information confidential; and/or is required by law to be disclosed. (b) During the Employment Term and for a period of two (2) years from the date of termination of Employee’s employment with PGS, Employee shall not: (i) serve as or become an employee, officer, director, shareholder, consultant, partner, owner, lender, principal, member, agent or otherwise, of any entity that is conducting or intends to conduct a business which is the same as or substantially similar to or competitive with the business of PGS; (ii) individually or with others solicit, attempt to obtain, divert or accept business from, or perform any service for, any client/customer of PGS; (iii) individually or with others, solicit or attempt to solicit, employ or retain any employees, representatives or agents of PGS; or (iv) individually or with others solicit or attempt to solicit services of any supplier of PGS in connection with any business activity that competes with the business of PGS. For the purposes of this Section 7, a business shall be deemed to compete with the business of PGS if such business provides during the Employment Term and the same services that PGS provides at the time of Employee’s termination. As used herein, the term, PGS, shall include any subsidiary of PGS and any successor to PGS or any such subsidiaries. (c) Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing contained in this Agreement shall prohibit Employee from purchasing and holding as an investment not more than 5% of any class of the issued and outstanding and publicly traded (on a recognized national or regional securities exchange or in the over-the-counter market) security of any corporation, partnership or other business entity that conducts a business in competition with PGS and of which he is not a consultant, employee, officer, or director. (d) Employee is agreeing to these provisions in consideration of the Agreement of PGS to enter into the other provisions of this Agreement. (e) Employee agrees that any claim for breach of this Section 7 against Employee may be brought by PGS, or any subsidiary or affiliate of PGS in lieu of PGS. Employee shall not raise any failure of PGS or any such subsidiary or affiliate to qualify as a foreign corporation to conduct business in any given jurisdiction as a defense to any action brought by PGS or any such subsidiary or affiliate. 4 (f) Employee acknowledges and agrees that the covenants contained in this Section 7 are fair and reasonable and of a special unique character which gives them peculiar value and PGS would not have entered into this Agreement without such covenants being made. However, if any such covenants shall be determined by any court to be invalid by reason of their duration or geographical scope, such duration or geographic scope, or both, as the case may be, shall be considered to be reduced to the longest duration or greatest geographic scope, or both, which will cure such invalidity. Employee further acknowledges that monetary damages alone will not be an adequate remedy for any breach by him of any of the covenants contained in this Section 7, and accordingly, Employee expressly agrees that, in addition to all other remedies which PGS has, PGS shall be entitled to injunctive relief, both preliminary and permanent, in any court of competent jurisdiction and shall not be required to post a bond or other security in connection with any such action. (g) Employee acknowledges that the limitations set forth in this Section 7 shall not prevent Employee from earning a livelihood after Employee leaves PGS’s employ but simply prevent unfair competition against PGS for a limited period. 8. Patents; Copyrights . Any interest in patents, patent applications, inventions, copyrights, developments, and processes (“Inventions”) which Employee during the period he is employed by PGS under this Agreement may develop relating to the fields in which PGS may then be engaged shall belong to PGS; and forthwith upon request of PGS and at no cost to PGS, Employee shall execute all such assignments and other documents and take all such other action as PGS may reasonably request in order to vest in PGS all of Employee’s right, title, and interest in and to such Inventions, free and clear of all liens, charges, and encumbrances. 9. Termination . (a) Employee may not be terminated by PGS except for Cause prior to the end of the Term. For purposes of this Agreement, “Cause” means any of the following: (i) Employee engaging in any acts of fraud, theft, or embezzlement in connection with the performance of Employee’s duties hereunder; (ii) Employee’s conviction for any felony, including any plea of guilty or nolo contendere; and/or (iii) Employee providing services, in any capacity, to a business that is in direct competition with PGS. (b) In the event that Employee shall be physically or mentally incapacitated or disabled or otherwise unable fully to discharge Employee’s essential duties hereunder, with or without reasonable accommodations, for a period of three (3) months (a “Permanent Disability”), then this Agreement may be terminated by PGS, in its sole discretion, upon the expiration of such three (3) month period, at which time the terms of Section 9 shall apply. In such event, PGS shall continue to pay Employee’s Salary as in effect at the time of such disability for a period of three (3) months from the date of such disability; provided , that such amounts shall be offset by any amounts otherwise paid to Employee under PGS’s then-existing disability program, if any. Unless otherwise provided for pursuant to Section 4(b) hereof, Employee shall be responsible for obtaining Employee’s own disability insurance policy, however, PGS may elect, in the sole and absolute discretion of the Board of Managers, to supplement such disability policy. 5 (d) In the event that Employee shall die, then this Agreement shall terminate on the date of Employee’s death, and no post-death compensation shall be payable to Employee hereunder, except for earned but unpaid Salary, earned bonuses, vested benefits, if any, and as may otherwise be provided under this Agreement. (e) In the event that this Agreement is terminated for Cause pursuant to Section 9(a), then Employee shall be entitled to receive only Employee’s Base Salary at the rate provided in Section 3 to the date on which termination shall take effect and payment of any accrued but unpaid bonuses earned, accrued vacation pay any another vested benefits. (f) In the event Employee voluntarily resigns from PGS during the Employment Term, this Agreement shall terminate effective upon the date such termination shall take effect and Employee shall be entitled to receive only Employee’s Salary to the date on which the termination shall take effect and payment of any accrued but unpaid bonuses earned, accrued vacation pay and any other vested benefits. 10. Separation Pay If the Employment Agreement is terminated (i) by PGS without Cause (including as a result of the Employee’s death or Disability), (ii) by Employee for Good Reason, or (iii) the Employment Term is not renewed by PGS at the end of the Employment Term, then PGS shall: (i) continue to pay to the Employee one-twelfth (1/12) of the annual Base Salary each month for a twelve month (12) month period commencing on the first scheduled payroll date immediately following the Termination Date, at the rate in effect at the time of termination, payable in accordance with PGS’s normal payroll practices; (ii) pay to Employee a single lump sum payment of all accrued but unpaid bonuses earned, such amount payable on the first scheduled payroll date immediately following the Termination Date; (iii) pay to Employee a single lump sum payment of all accrued but unpaid vacation pay or other benefits earned; and (iv) to the extent unvested, fully accelerate the vesting of any outstanding options or equity grants such that all outstanding options and/or equity grants are fully vested as of the Termination Date. For purposes hereof, “Good Reason” shall mean any one of the following: (i) the material reduction of Employee’s (a) Base Salary from one year of the Employment Term to another, and/or (b) Bonus Milestones and/or bonus potential ; (ii) the material reduction of Employee’s duties and responsibilities as set forth herein (including material reduction in status, and/or a requirement to report to any person or entity other than the Board of Managers of PGS and the CEO of the Corporation; (iii) PGS’s material breach of this Agreement; or (iv) a change in Employee’s place of work outside of the San Antonio-New Braunfels metropolitan area . 6 Employee will not be deemed to have Good Reason unless (i) Employee first provides the Board with written notice of the condition giving rise to Good Reason within thirty (30) days of its initial occurrence (ii) PGS fails to cure such condition within thirty (30) days after receiving such written notice (the “Cure Period”), and (iii) Employee’s resignation based on such Good Reason is effective within thirty (30) days after the expiration of the Cure Period. 11. Dispute Resolution . In the event of any dispute arising out of this Agreement, whether such dispute gives rise to a cause of action sounding in contract and/or tort, and/or whether based on a statute or case law, including, without limitation, the breach of the covenant of “good faith” and “fair dealing,” or otherwise, the parties agree to submit any and all such dispute(s) (if any) to final and binding arbitration pursuant to the Rules of the American Arbitration Association with the venue of all arbitration hearing(s) to be in San Antonio, Texas, or such other place(s) within the State of Texas as the parties may agree to in writing. Judgment upon the award rendered by the arbitrator may be entered in any Texas court having jurisdiction thereof. Each party shall be responsible for its own fees and expenses associated with the arbitration and the parties shall equally share the costs of the arbitration. 12. Merger, Etc . In the event of a future disposition of the properties and business of PGS, substantially as an entirety, by merger, consolidation, sale of assets, sale of stock, or otherwise (each, a “Change of Control Event”), then PGS may elect to assign this Agreement and all of its rights and obligations hereunder to the acquiring or surviving entity provided that the acquiring or surviving entity agrees in writing to be bound by the terms and conditions of this Agreement, or, in the event this Agreement is not assigned and/or the surviving entity does not agree to be bound by the terms and conditions of this Agreement, then the Employee shall be entitled to receive a lump sum payment immediately upon the Change of Control Event, in amount equal to the remaining Base Salary under the Employment Term and any accrued but unpaid bonuses, vacation pay and other benefits. Moreover, any unvested equity grants, whether in the form of options, profit interests or other equity instrument, will automatically become fully vested upon any Change of Control Event irrespective of whether or not this Agreement is assumed by an acquiring or surviving entity. 13. Survival . The covenants, agreements, representations, and warranties contained in or made pursuant to this Agreement shall survive Employee’s termination of employment, irrespective of any investigation made by or on behalf of any party. 14. Entire Agreement and Modification . This Agreement, set forth the entire understanding of the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, supersede all existing agreements between them concerning such subject matter, and may be modified only by a written instrument duly executed by each party. 7 15. Notices . Any notice or other communication required or permitted to be given hereunder shall be in writing and shall be mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested (or by the most nearly comparable method if mailed from or to a location outside of the United States) or by Federal Express, Express Mail, or similar overnight delivery, or courier service or delivered in person, by email or by facsimile, or similar telecommunications equipment against receipt to the party to whom it is to be given at the address of such party set forth in this Section 15 (or to such other address as the party shall have furnished in writing in accordance with the provisions of this Section 15). Employee: Michael Wanke [*] [*] (C) [*] (E) [*] PGS: Patriot Glass Solutions, LLC c/o Transportation and Logistics Systems, Inc. 110 Chestnut Ridge Rd., Suite 444 Montvale, NJ 07645 Attn.: Sebastian Giordano (C) [*] (E) [*] Such addresses may be changed by notice given as provided in this Section 15. Notices shall be effective upon the date of receipt; provided, however, that a notice (other than a notice of a changed address) sent by certified or registered U.S. mail, with postage prepaid, shall be presumed received no later than three (3) business days following the date of sending. 16. Waiver . Any waiver by either party of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate as or be construed to be a waiver of any other breach of such provision or of any breach of any other provision of this Agreement. The failure of a party to insist upon strict adherence to any term of this Agreement on one or more occasions shall not be considered a waiver or deprive that party of the right thereafter to insist upon strict adherence to that term or any other term of this Agreement. Any waiver must be in writing and signed by the party providing such waiver. 17. Binding Effect . Employee’s rights and obligations under this Agreement shall not be transferable by assignment or otherwise, such rights shall not be subject to encumbrance or the claims of Employee’s creditors, and any attempt to do any of the foregoing shall be void. The provisions of this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Employee and Employee’s heirs and personal representatives and shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of PGS and its successors and those who are its assigns. 18. Headings . The headings in this Agreement are solely for the convenience of reference and shall be given no effect in the construction or interpretation of this Agreement. 19. Governing Law . This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Texas, without giving effect to such State’s rules governing the conflicts of laws. Venue shall be in Bexar County, Texas. 20. Counterparts; Electronic Transmission . This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts. All executed counterparts shall constitute one agreement notwithstanding that all signatories are not signatories to the original or the same counterpart. Any signature page delivered by electronic transmission, such as facsimile or via email with a pdf attachment of such signed signature page, shall be binding to the same extent as an original signature page, with regard to any agreement subject to the terms hereof or any amendment thereto. IN WITNESS WHEREOF , the parties have duly executed this Agreement as of the date first written above. text: EX-10.8 12 ex10-8.htm EX-10.8 Exhibit 10.8 FIRST AMENDMENT TO COMMERCIAL LEASE AGREEMENT This FIRST AMENDMENT TO COMMERCIAL LEASE AGREEMENT (this “First Amendment”) is entered into effective as of November 1, 2026 (the “First Amendment Effective Date”), by and between MDW Management, LLC, a Texas limited liability company (“Landlord”) and Patriot Glass Solutions, LLC, a Texas limited liability company (the “Tenant”). RECITALS WHEREAS , Landlord and Tenant, under its prior name, Mobile Tint, LLC, a Texas limited liability company, d/b/a A-1 Glass, entered into that certain Commercial Lease Agreement on or about July 21, 2021, but effective as of April 19, 2021 (the “Lease”), pursuant to which Landlord leased the building, grounds, land and improvements known as 2029 Pat Booker Road, Universal City, Texas 78148, and more particularly identified as the “Leased Premises” (as defined in the Lease) to Tenant. All capitalized terms used herein but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Lease. WHEREAS , the members of Tenant at the time of the effective date of the Lease, were C-Bond Systems, Inc., a Colorado corporation (“C-Bond”), which owned an eighty (80%) percent member interest in Tenant and Michael Wanke (“Mr. Wanke”), who owned a twenty (20%) percent member interest in Tenant; WHEREAS , pursuant to a certain Debt Forgiveness, Equity Redemption and Strict Foreclosure Agreement dated as of January 30, 2025, by and among, (i) C-Bond, (ii) C-Bond Systems, LLC, a Texas limited liability company and a wholly owned subsidiary of C-Bond (“C-Bond LLC”), (iii) Tenant, (iv) Badcer Ops, Inc., a Nevada corporation (“Badcer”), (v) Jeff Badders (“Mr. Badders”), (vi) Badders Children’s Trust (“Badders Trust”), (vii) Mercer Street Global Opportunity Fund, LLC (“Mercer”) and (viii) Mr. Wanke, pursuant to which, among other things, the eighty (80%) percent ownership interest in Tenant owned by C-Bond, was assigned to Badcer, with the remaining twenty (20%) ownership interest in Tenant continuing to be owned by Mr. Wanke; WHEREAS , Tenant has entered into a certain Member Interest and Asset Exchange Agreement dated as of April 1, 2026, as amended by and among (i) Transportation and Logistics Systems, Inc., a Nevada corporation (“TLSS”), (ii) TLSS Acquisition, Inc., a Delaware corporation, and a wholly-owned subsidiary of TLSS (“TA”), (iii) TLSS Reverse PGS, LLC, a Texas limited liability company, a wholly owned subsidiary of TA (“Reverse”), (iv) Badcer, (v) Badders, (vi) Mercer, (vii) Tenant and (viii) Mr. Wanke (collectively, the “Exchange Agreement”), pursuant to which Tenant, through a reverse triangular merger with Reverse, shall be the surviving entity, and upon consummation of the closing of the Exchange Agreement, Tenant shall be owned twenty (20%) percent by Mr. Wanke and eighty (80%) percent of Tenant shall be owned by TA; and WHEREAS , in connection with the closing of the Exchange Agreement, Landlord and Tenant desire to enter into this First Amendment to the Lease in order to amend certain terms and provisions of the Lease. NOW, THEREFORE , for and in consideration of ten and No/100 Dollar ($10.00) and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, Landlord and Tenant hereby recite and agree as follows: 1. Recitals . The recitals are true, accurate and correct and are expressly incorporated herein. 2. Fundamental Lease Provisions . a. Tenant . From and after the First Amendment Effective Date, all references in the Lease to the “Tenant” means Patriot Glass Solutions, LLC, as owned eighty (80%) percent by TA and twenty (20%) percent by Mr. Wanke. b. Permitted Use . The Permitted Use includes window tint solutions for auto, home and business owners, specializing in automotive window tinting, residential window film and commercial window film that stop harmful UV rays from passing through its window films for reduced glare, comfortable temperatures and lower energy bills, as well as products that offer forced-entry protection and films that protect glass from scratches, graffiti, other types of vandalism, and even bullets, including C-Bond BRS, a ballistic-resistant film system. c. Lease Term . Upon full execution hereof, Landlord hereby accepts Tenant’s exercise of Tenant’s first five (5) year option to renew the Primary Lease Term, referenced in the Fundamental Lease Provisions, Section 4 and Section II, entitled Term , subsection (c) of the Lease. The Parties agree that the original Commencement Date and Rent Commencement Date was April 19, 2021, and the revised Lease Term, after having exercised its first five (5) year option to renew, shall now end on April 19, 2031. Landlord hereby acknowledges that Tenant has one remaining five (5) year option to renew the Lease. 1 d. Insurance Payments . As the Tenant is paying for the insurance coverages set forth in Section 9 of the Lease, entitled Casualty Losses and Destruction of Premises , subsection (f), insurance payments shall not be part of the Additional Rent payable to the Landlord and all references to “Insurance Payment” as set forth in the Lease, including, but not limited to Section 19 of the Lease, entitled Additional Rent , are hereby deleted. e. Confirmation of Rent . During the first extended the Lease Term (as extended and renewed by this First Amendment), the Monthly Minimum Rent is $5,600 (and that such Minimum Rent shall not increase 2% commencing over the initial Lease Term) and Additional Rent is $1,258.20 per month, consisting of real estate taxes based on 2025 taxes, for a combined Monthly Rent total of $6,858.20. Each Lease Year during the remaining Lease Term, commencing as of May 1, the Monthly Rent shall be adjusted for the actual real estate taxes based upon the actual real estate bill, however, Monthly Minimum Rent shall remain $5,600 for the current Lease Term. f. Notices . The “Mandatory Copy To” notice shown in Section 1 of the Fundamental Lease Provisions, is hereby amended to read: CJMA Business Law and Litigation, Attn K. “Andy” Tiwari, Esq., 111 W. Sunset Rd., San Antonio, TX 78209, Email: andy.tiwari@cjma.law. g. Guarantor . Section 10 of the Fundamental Lease Provisions, entitled Guarantors, is hereby deleted in its entirety and replaced with “Intentionally Deleted”. 3. Change of Control . Landlord consents to a one-time change in ownership or control of Tenant that would otherwise constitute an impermissible assignment under Section VI of the Lease, entitled Assignment and Subletting, provided that the change in ownership or control is completed in accordance with the Exchange Agreement. Landlord is not waiving any right to enforce Section VI of the Lease for events arising after the Effective Date or changes in control that are inconsistent with the Exchange Agreement. 4. Corporate Guaranty . The Guaranty attached as Exhibit A-1 to the Lease is hereby cancelled as of the Effective Date, and the Lease will no longer carry a guaranty. Notwithstanding any residual Lease language referencing a “guarantor,” the Lease shall be interpreted and construed consistent with the removal of the Guaranty as of the First Amendment Effective Date. 5. Other Terms . Except as expressly modified by this First Amendment, the Lease remains unchanged and in full force and effect. In the event of a conflict between the terms of the Lease and this First Amendment, the terms of this First Amendment shall control. From and after the First Amendment Effective Date, any reference to “ Lease ” will mean the Lease as amended by this First Amendment. 6. Landlord Estoppel . Landlord hereby represents and warrants to Tenant as of this First Amendment Effective Date that: a. Landlord is the fee simple owner of the Leased Premises; b. Landlord is leasing the entire Leased Premises to the Tenant; c. By entering into this First Amendment, Landlord shall not be in default of any other agreement that Landlord is a party to, including any mortgage or deed of trust, encumbering the Leased Premises; d. Landlord is not in default under any mortgage or deed of trust encumbering the Leased Premises; e. Landlord hereby acknowledges and agrees that neither Tenant, nor its predecessors-in-interest are in default under the terms of the Lease, as amended and that there are no uncured events of default that are continuing, and no amount of Monthly Rent is due for any periods prior to the effective date of this First Amendment; f. Landlord hereby agrees that Tenant does not owe Landlord any money in connection with the preparation of this First Amendment; g. Landlord has no knowledge of the presence of any recognized environmental conditions on, about or impacting the Leased Premises; h. Landlord has no knowledge of any permits that Tenant is required to obtain in order to operate its business at the Leased Premises; and 2 i. Landlord hereby agrees that there are no brokers involved in the negotiation of this First Amendment and in the event any brokers are entitled to any fees or commissions with respect to the Lease and/or this First Amendment, Landlord shall solely be responsible for the same and Landlord shall indemnify, defend and hold tenant harmless with respect to any claims by any brokers with respect to the Lease and/or this First Amendment. 7. Miscellaneous . a. Authority . Each party has the full legal authority to execute and deliver this First Amendment. b. Multiple Counterparts . Multiple copies of this First Amendment may be executed by the parties hereto. Each such executed copy shall have the full force and effect of an original executed instrument. Signatures submitted by scanned attachment to electronic mail or via digital signatures shall be considered originals. IN WITNESS WHEREOF , the Landlord and Tenant have executed this First Amendment as of the dates set forth below. LANDLORD: TENANT: MDW Management LLC, a Texas Patriot Glass Solutions LLC, a Texas limited liability company limited liability company ( f/k/a Mobile Tint LLC ) By: /s/ Michael Wanke By: /s/ Sebastian Giordano Name: Michael Wanke Name: Sebastian Giordano Title: Authorized Member Title: Authorized Manager Date: November 1, 2026 Date: November 1, 2026 3

text: EX-10.1 3 ea031085601ex10-1.htm AMENDMENT NO. 7 TO CREDIT AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO GUARANTEE AND COLLATERAL AGREEMENT, DATED AS OF NOVEMBER 3, 2026, AMONG BRC GROUP HOLDINGS, INC Exhibit 10.1 EXECUTION VERSION AMENDMENT NO. 7 TO CREDIT AGREEMENT AND AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO GUARANTEE AND COLLATERAL AGREEMENT This AMENDMENT NO. 7 TO CREDIT AGREEMENT and AMENDMENT NO. 2 to GUARANTEE AND COLLATERAL AGREEMENT (this “ Amendment ”) is entered into effective November 3, 2026 (the “ Amendment No. 7 Effective Date ”), among BRC Group Holdings, Inc. (f/k/a B. Riley Financial, Inc.), a Delaware corporation (the “ Ultimate Parent ”), BR Financial Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “ Borrower ”), each of the other Loan Parties party hereto, each of the lenders party hereto (the “ Lenders ”) and Oaktree Fund Administration, LLC, as administrative agent for the Lenders (in such capacity, together with its successors and permitted assigns in such capacity, the “ Administrative Agent ”) and as collateral agent (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns in such capacity, the “ Collateral Agent ”). All capitalized terms used herein (including in this preamble) and not otherwise defined herein shall have the respective meanings provided such terms in the Credit Agreement referred to below. R E C I T A L S : WHEREAS, the Ultimate Parent, the Borrower, the other Loan Parties party thereto, the Lenders, the Administrative Agent, and the Collateral Agent are parties to that certain Credit Agreement, dated as of February 26, 2025 (as amended by Amendment No. 1 to Credit Agreement and Guarantee and Collateral Agreement, dated as of March 24, 2025, as amended by Amendment No. 2 to Credit Agreement, dated as of July 8, 2025, as amended by Amendment No. 3 to Credit Agreement, dated as of October 8, 2025, as amended by Amendment No. 4 to Credit Agreement, dated as of January 14, 2026, as amended by Amendment No. 5 to Credit Agreement, dated as of August 7, 2026, as amended by Amendment No. 6 to Credit Agreement, Consent and Waiver, dated as of September 28, 2026, and as further amended, restated, amended and restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time prior to the date hereof, the “ Credit Agreement ”); WHEREAS, the Ultimate Parent, the Borrower, the other Loan Parties party thereto, the Administrative Agent, and the Collateral Agent are parties to that certain Guarantee and Collateral Agreement, dated as of February 26, 2025 (as amended by Amendment No. 1 to Credit Agreement and Guarantee and Collateral Agreement, dated as of March 24, 2025, and as further amended, restated, amended and restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time prior to the date hereof, the “ Guarantee and Collateral Agreement ”); WHEREAS, pursuant to Section 9.01 of the Credit Agreement, the Ultimate Parent and the Borrower have requested the Administrative Agent and the Lenders agree to amend the Credit Agreement as hereinafter provided; WHEREAS, the Borrower, the Administrative Agent and the Lenders have agreed, subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein and in the Credit Agreement, to establish a new tranche of incremental Term Loan Commitments (the “ Amendment No. 7 Term Loan Commitments ” and any term loans made in respect thereof, the “ Amendment No. 7 Term Loans ”) in an aggregate principal amount of $26,500,000; WHEREAS, the Borrower has requested, and each Person identified on Annex A.1 attached hereto as an “ Amendment No. 7 Term Lender ” (each, an “ Amendment No. 7 Term Lender ”) has agreed, to provide on the Amendment No. 7 Effective Date, immediately after giving effect to the transactions described in Section 4 below, the Amendment No. 7 Term Loan Commitments available to the Borrower in the amount set forth opposite such Person’s name on Annex A.1 attached hereto, which Amendment No. 7 Term Loan Commitments shall have the same terms as the existing Term Loan Commitments under the Credit Agreement except as otherwise set forth in this Amendment and the Credit Agreement as amended by this Amendment; and WHEREAS, subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein, the Administrative Agent and the Lenders party hereto are willing to agree to such amendments, all as hereinafter provided. NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows: Section 1. Rules of Construction . The rules of construction specified in Section 1.02 of the Credit Agreement shall apply to this Amendment, including the terms defined in the preamble and recitals hereto. Section 2. Transaction Fee . The parties hereto agree that, immediately after giving effect to this Amendment and immediately prior to giving effect to the transactions described in Section 3 below and the Amendment No. 7 Term Lenders making available the Amendment No. 7 Term Loan Commitments, as consideration for the agreements of the Lenders party hereto, the Borrower shall pay to the Administrative Agent, for the ratable benefit of each Lender, a transaction fee equal to $3,281,250.00 (the “ Transaction Fee ”), which Transaction Fee shall be fully earned and non-refundable, and due and payable in full on the Amendment No. 7 Effective Date and which shall be paid-in-kind by capitalizing and adding such Transaction Fee to the aggregate outstanding principal balance of Initial Term Loans on the Amendment No. 7 Effective Date (which shall thereafter bear interest in accordance with Section 2.14 of the Credit Agreement, as amended by this Amendment) (such payment, the “ Transaction Fee Payment ”). Section 3. Great American Holdings, LLC Equity Interests . The parties hereto agree that, immediately after giving effect to the Transaction Fee Payment, as a result of arms-length negotiations between certain Lenders party hereto (the “ Purchasing Lenders ”) and the Borrower, the Purchasing Lenders shall purchase (the “ Purchase ”) certain Equity Interests of Great American Holdings, LLC pursuant to that certain Membership Interest Purchase Agreement, dated as of the Amendment No. 7 Effective Date (the “ Equity Purchase Agreement ”), by, among others, the Purchasing Lenders, the Purchasers (as defined in the Equity Purchase Agreement) and BRF Finance Co., LLC. Section 4. Prepayment . The parties hereto agree that, immediately after giving effect to the transactions described in Section 3 above, the Borrower shall voluntarily prepay Initial Term Loans in an aggregate principal amount of $51,679,687.50 (the “ Prepaid Term Loans ”). Notwithstanding anything herein or in the Credit Agreement to the contrary (including Section 2.05 of the Credit Agreement), (i) the Prepaid Term Loans shall not be subject to, nor shall such voluntary prepayment described in this Section 4 trigger, the required payment of the Prepayment Premium, (ii) all accrued and unpaid interest on the Prepaid Term Loans shall be due and payable on the Amendment No. 7 Effective Date and (iii) this Amendment shall satisfy the notice of voluntary prepayment to the Administrative Agent and the Lenders required by Section 2.09(b) of the Credit Agreement. Section 5. Amendment No. 7 Term Loans . text: EX-10.34 2 e8044_ex10-34.htm EXHIBIT 10.34 EXHIBIT 10.34 SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT – COMMON STOCK No Camera Films, Inc. 9454 Wilshire Blvd., PH 37 Beverly Hills CA, 90212 Re: Offering of Common Stock of No Camera Films, Inc., a Wyoming corporation (the Company) 1. Subscription. The undersigned hereby applies to purchase shares of the Company’s voting common stock (the “Common Stock”) indicated below in accordance with the terms of this Subscription Agreement and the private placement relating to the offering of the Common Stock by the Company (the “Offering”). Herein the terms “Stock” shall mean the Common Stock. The Share Price is $.20 per share (twenty cents per share). The undersigned hereby irrevocably offers to purchase 5,000,000 shares of the Common Stock for the total consideration of $1,000,000 (One Million Dollars), and therefore tenders, as the total consideration for the purchase of the Stock, a promissory note in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A, payable to Mindatorium, Inc., the controlling shareholder of the Company, which will cause the Company to issue the Stock. The executed promissory note will be delivered to Mindatorium, Inc. within three business days of the undersigned signing this subscription agreement. It is understood that the promissory note tendered is irrevocable by the undersigned, and that the obligations under it are payable to Mindatorium, Inc. in accordance with its terms. All currency referenced is US dollars. 2. Representations and Warranties of the Investor. The undersigned represents and warrants as follows: (a) The undersigned has received information provided to him/her/her in writing by the Company, or information from books and records of the Company. The undersigned understands that all documents, records and books pertaining to this investment have been made available for inspection by him/her, his attorney and/or his/her accountant and/or his/her “Purchaser Representative” as defined in Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and that the books and records of the Company will be available, upon reasonable notice, for inspection by investors during reasonable business hours at the Company’s principal place of business. The undersigned and/or his/her advisers have had a reasonable opportunity to ask questions of and receive answers from the Company, or a person or persons acting on its behalf, concerning the Offering, and all such questions have been answered to the full satisfaction of the undersigned. No oral representations have been made, and to the extent oral information has been furnished to the undersigned or his/her advisers in connection with the Offering, such information was consistent with all written information furnished. (b) The undersigned (i) has adequate means of providing for his/her current needs and possible personal contingencies, (ii) has no need for liquidity in this investment, (iii) is able to bear the economic risks of an investment in the Stock for an indefinite period, and (iv) at the present time, could afford a complete loss of such investment. (c) The undersigned recognizes that the Company has a limited financial and operating history and no history of profitable operations, and that the Stock as an investment involves special risks, including those disclosed to the undersigned by the Company. (d) The undersigned understands that the Stock has not been nor will be registered under the Securities Act or the securities laws of any state, in reliance upon an exemption therefrom for non-public offerings. The undersigned further understands that the Company is under no obligation to register the Stock on his/her behalf or to assist him/her in complying with any exemption from registration. (e) The Stock is being purchased solely for his/her own account for investment and not for the account of any other person and not for distribution, assignment, or resale to others and no other person has a direct or indirect beneficial interest in the Stock. The undersigned or his/her advisers have such knowledge and experience in financial, tax, and business matters to enable him/her to utilize the information made available to him/her in connection with the Offering to evaluate the merits and risks of the prospective investment and to make an informed investment decision with respect thereto. (f) The undersigned, if a corporation, partnership, trusts, or other entity, is authorized and otherwise duly qualified to purchase and hold the Stock. (g) All information which the undersigned has provided to the Company concerning himself, his/her financial position, and his/her knowledge of financial and business matters, or in the case of a corporation, partnership, trust or other entity, the knowledge of financial and business matters of the person making the investment decision on behalf of such entity is correct and complete as of the date set forth at the end hereof, and if there should be any adverse change in such information prior to his/her subscription being accepted, he will immediately provide the Company with such information. (h) The undersigned understands and agrees that the following restrictions and limitations are applicable to his/her purchase and his/her resales, hypothecations or other transfers of the Stock pursuant to Regulation D under the Securities Act: (i) The undersigned agrees that the Stock shall not be sold, pledged, hypothecated or otherwise transferred unless the shares of the Stock are registered under the Securities Act, and the securities laws of any state or is exempt therefrom; (ii) The shares represented by this certificate have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or any applicable state securities laws. The shares represented by this certificate may not be transferred, sold, or assigned unless so registered, or unless an exemption from such registration is available. (iii) Transfer of the shares represented by this certificate is subject to the restrictions in the corporation’s bylaws. Stop transfer instructions to the transfer agent of the Stock have been or will be placed with respect to the Stock so as to restrict the resale, pledge, hypothecation or other transfer thereof, subject to the further items hereof, including the provisions of the legend set forth in subparagraph (ii) above; and (iv) The legend and stop transfer instructions described in subparagraphs (ii) and (iii) above will be placed with respect to any new certificate(s) or other document(s) issued upon presentment by the undersigned of certificate(s) or other document(s) for transfer. (i) The undersigned understands that neither the Securities and Exchange Commission nor the securities commission of any state has made any finding or determination relating to the fairness for public investment in the Stock and that the Securities and Exchange Commission as well as the securities commission of any state will not recommend or endorse any offering of securities. (j) The undersigned acknowledges and is aware that it never has been represented, guaranteed, or warranted to him/her by the Company, its directors, officers, agents or employees, or any other person, expressly or by implication, that the limited past performance or experience on the part of the Company, or any future projections will in any way indicate the predictable results of the ownership of the Stock or of the overall financial performance of the Company. (k) (Complete if applicable) The undersigned acknowledges that ________________ has acted as the “Purchaser Representative” as defined in Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act, and (i) that he can bear the economic risk of this investment; (ii) he has relied upon the advice of the Purchaser Representative as to the merits of an investment in the Company and the suitability of such investment for the undersigned; and (iii) the Purchaser Representative has confirmed to him/her, in writing, any past, present or future material relationship, actual or contemplated, between the Purchaser representative or its affiliates and the Company or its affiliates. (l) The undersigned acknowledges that the Company has made available to him/her or the Purchaser Representative, if any, or other personal advisers the opportunity to obtain additional information to verify the accuracy of the information furnished to him/her and to evaluate the merits and risks of this investment. (m) The undersigned confirms that he has consulted with the Purchaser Representative, if any, or other personal advisers and that the Purchaser Representative or other advisers have analyzed the information furnished to him/her and the documents relating thereto on his/her behalf and have advised him/her of the business and financial aspects and consequences of and potential liabilities associated with his/her investment in the Stock. The undersigned represents that he has made other risk capital investments or other investments of a speculative nature, and by reason of his/her business and financial experience and of the business and financial experience of those persons he has retained to advise him/her with respect to investments of this nature. In reaching the conclusion that he desires to acquire the Stock, the undersigned has carefully evaluated his/her financial resources and investments and acknowledges that he is able to bear the economic risks of this investment. (n) The undersigned acknowledges that all information made available to him/her and/or the Purchaser Representative, if any, and/or personal advisers in connection with his/her investment in the Stock, including the information furnished to him/her, is and shall remain confidential in all respects and may not be reproduced, distributed or used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of the Company. (o) Capitalization. The undersigned acknowledges that the Company is a Wyoming corporation and that, as of the date hereof and prior to the Offering, the Company is wholly owned by Mindatorium, Inc. The Company is authorized to issue 100,000,000 shares of voting Common Stock, of which 60,000,000 shares have been issued to Mindatorium, Inc. The undersigned is purchasing 5,000,000 newly issued shares of the Common Stock for the total consideration of $1,000,000, which shall be paid by the promissory note attached hereto as Exhibit A, payable to Mindatorium, Inc. Upon the issuance of such shares, 65,000,000 shares of the Common Stock will be outstanding, of which the undersigned will hold 5,000,000 shares (approximately 7.69%) and Mindatorium, Inc. will hold 60,000,000 shares (approximately 92.31%), and 35,000,000 shares will remain authorized but unissued. Mindatorium, Inc. will retain controlling voting ownership of the Company. (p) Dilution. The undersigned acknowledges and agrees that the remaining 35,000,000 authorized but unissued shares of the Common Stock will be issued over time to future investors or, if no such investors subscribe, to Mindatorium, Inc., at such times and on such terms as the Company may determine, without further consent of the undersigned. The undersigned understands that as such shares are issued, his/her percentage ownership of the Company will decrease from approximately 7.69% at the closing of the Offering to 5.00% when all 100,000,000 authorized shares have been issued, and that the number of shares of the Stock held by the undersigned, 5,000,000 shares, will not change as a result of such issuances. The undersigned acknowledges that this dilution is the intended and agreed outcome of the Offering. (q) Valuation. The undersigned acknowledges that the Share Price of $.20 per share reflects a post-money valuation of the Company of $20,000,000 on a fully issued basis of 100,000,000 shares of the Common Stock, that such valuation and the Share Price were determined by the Company, and that no independent appraisal or valuation of the Company or the Stock has been obtained. (r) Related Party and Control. The undersigned acknowledges that the Company is a subsidiary controlled by Mindatorium, Inc., that Mindatorium, Inc. will retain controlling voting ownership of the Company and will be able to control matters requiring the approval of the Company’s shareholders, and that the Company and Mindatorium, Inc. may have officers and directors in common, which may give rise to conflicts of interest. The undersigned further acknowledges that the purchase of the Stock does not entitle him/her to a seat on the Company’s board of directors or to any special rights, preferences or privileges, unless separately agreed in writing by the Company. (s) Use of Proceeds. The undersigned acknowledges that the proceeds of the Offering will be received by Mindatorium, Inc. and applied for the Company’s benefit to expand production toward approximately 20 personnel, establish a headquarters in Los Angeles, build sales and marketing, fund customer acquisition, produce and distribute Company-owned films and series, continue technology and intellectual property development, including the Company’s patent-pending process, support international expansion, and provide working capital, and that the Company shall have broad discretion in the application of such proceeds. (t) Additional Risks. The undersigned acknowledges that an investment in the Stock involves risks in addition to those described elsewhere in this Subscription Agreement, including the following: (i) The Company is an early-stage company, and its business, operations and prospects are subject to the risks and uncertainties inherent in a new business enterprise; (ii) Any projections, estimates, pipeline figures or planning scenarios furnished to the undersigned are estimates only, are based on assumptions that may not prove accurate, and are not guarantees of future results; (iii) The Company’s business depends on artificial intelligence technologies, which are evolving rapidly and may become subject to new or changing laws, regulations and industry standards that could increase the Company’s costs or limit its operations; (iv) The Company’s success depends in part on its ability to protect its intellectual property, including its patent-pending process, and there can be no assurance that any patent will issue or that the Company’s intellectual property will not be challenged or infringed; (v) The Company depends on the continued services of its key personnel, including its Chief Executive Officer, and the loss of any such person could adversely affect the Company; and (vi) There is no public market for the Stock and none is expected to develop, and the Stock constitutes restricted securities that may not be resold except as described in this Subscription Agreement, so that the undersigned may be required to hold the Stock for an indefinite period. (u) Payment to Mindatorium, Inc. The undersigned acknowledges that the Company is a newly formed corporation and has no bank account, and that accordingly the promissory note attached hereto as Exhibit A is payable to, and the proceeds thereof will be received by, Mindatorium, Inc., which, as the controlling shareholder of the Company, will cause the issuance of the Stock on behalf of the Company. 3. The undersigned is an “Accredited Investor” as defined in Rule 501(a) of the Securities Act. Please check one. The undersigned is: _____ 3.1. a natural person whose individual net worth (i.e., excess of total assets over total liabilities), inclusive of home, home furnishings and automobiles, or joint net worth with that person’s spouse, at the time of his/her purchase of the Shares exceeds $1,000,000; _____ 3.2. a natural person who had an individual income in excess of $200,000 in each of the two most recent calendar years or joint income with that person’s spouse in excess of $300,000 in each of those years and has a reasonable expectation of reaching the same income level in the current year. Individual income is defined for this purpose as adjusted gross income as determined for federal income tax purposes under the Internal Revenue Code (the “Code”), plus (i) any deductions for long-term capital gains under Section 1202 of the Code, (ii) any depletion deductions under Section 611, et seq. , of the Code, (iii) any interest income excluded under Section 103 of the Code, and (iv) any partnership losses allocated to the undersigned as reported on Schedule E of Form 1040; _____ 3.3. a corporation, limited liability company, partnership, or a Massachusetts or similar business trust, which was not formed for the specific purpose of acquiring the Shares, with total assets in excess of $5,000,000; _____ 3.4. an entity in which all of the equity owners are “accredited investors.” 4. Indemnification. The undersigned agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against all damages, losses, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) which they may incur by reason of the failure of the undersigned to fulfill any of the terms or conditions of this subscription, or by reason of any breach of the representations and warranties made by the undersigned herein, or in any document provided by the undersigned to the Company. 5. Survival. The foregoing representations, warranties and undertakings are made with the intent that they may be relied upon in determining the undersigned’s suitability as an investor in the Company and the undersigned hereby agrees that such representations and warranties shall survive his/her purchase of the Stock. The undersigned hereby acknowledges and agrees that he is not entitled to cancel, terminate or revoke this Subscription Agreement, or any agreements hereunder, and that this Subscription Agreement and such agreements shall survive (a) changes in the transactions, documents, and instruments previously furnished to the undersigned which are not materially adverse, and (b) the undersigned’s death or disability. 6. Notices. All notices or other communications given or made hereunder shall be in writing and shall be delivered or mailed by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, to the undersigned or to the Company at the respective addresses set forth herein. 7. Miscellaneous. (a) Notwithstanding any of the representations, warranties, acknowledgments, or agreements made herein by the undersigned, the undersigned does not thereby or in any other manner waive any rights granted to the undersigned under federal or state securities laws. (b) Words of any gender used in this Subscription Agreement shall be held and construed to include any other gender, and words in the singular number shall be held to include the plural, and vice versa, unless the context requires otherwise. (c) [Reserved.] (d) This Subscription Agreement contains the entire understanding of the parties and may not be changed orally, but only by an instrument in writing signed by the party against whom enforcement of any waiver, change, modification, extension, or discharge is sought. (e) Arbitration. Any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation, or validity thereof, including the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be exclusively resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the following: (i) Governing Law and Forum. The arbitration shall be administered by JAMS pursuant to its Comprehensive Arbitration Rules and Procedures, and conducted in Los Angeles County, California, unless the parties mutually agree to a different location. The arbitration shall be conducted by a single neutral arbitrator experienced in corporate and securities matters. (ii) Rules and Procedures. The arbitrator shall have the authority to grant any relief that would be available in a court of competent jurisdiction. The arbitrator shall issue a reasoned written decision explaining the essential findings and conclusions on which the award is based. Judgment on the arbitration award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. (iii) Confidentiality. The parties agree that the arbitration proceedings, filings, disclosures, and award shall remain confidential to the maximum extent permitted by law. (iv) Waiver of Jury Trial. By signing this Agreement, the parties knowingly and voluntarily waive any right to a trial by jury or to participate in a class action related to any claims covered by this arbitration clause. (v) Costs and Attorneys’ Fees. The prevailing party in any arbitration or enforcement of the arbitration award shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys’ fees, costs, and expenses. (f) The undersigned agrees that he/she has read the executive summary and business plan provided by the company. 8. Instructions for Payment. The undersigned shall pay the Subscription Amount by delivery of the promissory note attached hereto as Exhibit A, payable to Mindatorium, Inc. The Company shall have no obligation to issue the Shares unless the promissory note has been delivered to Mindatorium, Inc.
