text: EX-10.35 3 e8044_ex10-35.htm EXHIBIT 10.35 EXHIBIT 10.35 NEITHER THIS NOTE NOR THE SECURITIES INTO WHICH IT MAY BE CONVERTED HAS BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED (THE “ SECURITIES ACT ”), OR ANY STATE SECURITIES LAW. THEY MAY NOT BE OFFERED, SOLD OR OTHERWISE TRANSFERRED IN THE ABSENCE OF AN EFFECTIVE REGISTRATION STATEMENT UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT AND APPLICABLE STATE LAW, OR AN AVAILABLE EXEMPTION FROM REGISTRATION. THE MAKER MAY REQUIRE AN OPINION OF COUNSEL, REASONABLY ACCEPTABLE TO THE MAKER, AS TO THE AVAILABILITY OF SUCH EXEMPTION. GBT TECHNOLOGIES INC. CONVERTIBLE PROMISSORY NOTE Term Detail Principal Amount $1,000,000.00 Original Issue Date November 5, 2026 Maturity Date One (1) year after the Original Issue Date Interest Rate 8% per annum, simple Conversion Price $0.10 per share, fixed, but for split adjustments Place of Issue Santa Monica, California GBT Technologies Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “ Maker ”), for value received, promises to pay to MINDATORIUM INC., a Wyoming corporation, qualified in California to conduct intra-state business, or its registered assigns (the “ Holder ”), the Principal Amount, together with interest as set out below, in lawful money of the United States of America. Purpose of this Note. This Note is issued as the purchase price, in whole or in part, for the Maker’s acquisition from the Holder of a five percent (5%) [membership / equity] interest (the “ Acquired Interest ”) in NO CAMERA FILMS, a Wyoming Corporation (the “ Target ”), under the NCF Subscription Agreement between the Maker and the Holder dated as of the Original Issue Date (the “ Purchase Agreement ”). This Note is a direct debt obligation of the Maker. SECTION 1. PRINCIPAL, INTEREST AND MATURITY 1.1 Interest. Interest accrues on the unpaid Principal Amount at eight percent (8%) per annum, simple, from the Original Issue Date until the Principal Amount is paid in full or converted. Interest is calculated on a 365-day year and the actual days elapsed. 1.2 Maturity. All unpaid principal and accrued interest are due and payable on the date that is one (1) year after the Original Issue Date (the “ Maturity Date ”), unless converted earlier under Section 2. 1.3 Prepayment. The Maker may prepay this Note, in whole or in part, only with the Holder’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, denied, or conditioned. Before any prepayment, after ten (10) business days’ written notice to the Holder, the Holder may convert all or part of the proposed prepayment amount under Section 2. 1.4 Application of Payments. Cash payments apply first to accrued and unpaid interest, then to the Principal Amount. 1.5 Usury Savings. Interest will never exceed the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Any excess is automatically reduced to that maximum, and any excess paid is credited to principal. 1.6 Business Days. A payment or obligation due on a day that is not a business day is due on the next business day. 1 SECTION 2. CONVERSION 2.1 Conversion Right. At any time and from time to time, from the Original Issue Date until this Note is paid or satisfied in full, the Holder may convert all or any part of the Conversion Amount into fully paid and non-assessable shares of the Maker’s common stock, par value $0.00001 per share, or any securities into which that stock is later reclassified or changed (the “ Common Stock ”). The conversion right survives the Maturity Date and any Event of Default until this Note is paid, converted, or satisfied under Section 3. 2.2 Conversion Amount. “ Conversion Amount ” means the principal being converted plus, at the Holder’s option, accrued and unpaid interest thereon through the Conversion Date. 2.3 Conversion Price. The conversion price is $0.10 per share (the “ Conversion Price ”). It is fixed. It does not reset to a market price or discount, and it does not change with the trading price of the Common Stock. 2.4 Reverse Splits. The Conversion Price will not be adjusted if, while this Note is outstanding, the Maker combines its outstanding Common Stock into fewer shares, whether by reverse stock split, share combination, or any reclassification, recapitalization or Fundamental Transaction having the same effect. For clarity, after any such event the Conversion Price remains $0.10 per post-event share. 2.5 Forward Splits and Stock Dividends. If, while this Note is outstanding, the Maker subdivides its Common Stock by forward split, or pays a dividend in Common Stock, the Conversion Price will be reduced proportionately, so the Holder receives the same proportion of the Maker’s equity it would have received before the event. 2.6 Number of Shares of Conversion Stock. The number of shares (the “ Conversion Stock ”) issuable on a conversion equals the Conversion Amount divided by the Conversion Price. Fractional shares are rounded up to the next whole share. 2.7 Notice and Conversion Date. The Holder converts by delivering a Notice of Conversion in the form of Exhibit A by e-mail or other written means. The “ Conversion Date ” is the date the notice is delivered, if delivered before 6:00 p.m. New York time on a business day; otherwise, it is the next business day. 2.8 Delivery of Shares. Within five (5) business days after the Conversion Date (the “ Share Delivery Date ”), the Maker instruct its transfer agent to deliver the shares of Conversion Stock to the prime broker specified by the Holder, electronically through DTC’s DWAC system if the shares are DWAC eligible, or otherwise in restricted book-entry form in the Holder’s name with the transfer agent. The Maker pays all transfer agent fees for same-day processing. If the Maker fails to instruct its transfer agent in accordance with the schedule required by Section 2.8, pursuant to a Notice of Conversion, and if after such date the Holder is required by its broker to purchase (in an open market transaction or otherwise) or the Holder’s brokerage firm otherwise purchases, Common Stock to deliver in satisfaction of a sale by the Holder of the shares of Conversion Stock that the Holder anticipated receiving upon such conversion (a “ Buy-In ”), then the Maker shall (A) pay in cash to the Holder the amount, if any, by which (x) the Holder’s total purchase price (including brokerage commissions, if any) for the Common Stock so purchased exceeds (y) the product of (1) the number of shares of Conversion Stock that the Company was required to deliver to the Holder in connection with the exercise at issue times (2) the price at which the sell order giving rise to such purchase obligation was executed, and (B) at the option of the Holder, either reinstate the portion of this Note and equivalent number of shares of Conversion Stock for which such conversion was not timely honored (in which case such conversion shall be deemed rescinded) or deliver to the Holder the number of shares of Conversion Stock that would have been issued had the Maker timely complied with its conversion obligations hereunder. The Holder shall provide the Maker written notice indicating the amounts payable to the Holder in respect of the Buy-In and, upon request of the Maker, evidence of the amount of such loss. Nothing herein shall limit the Holder’s right to pursue any other remedies available to it hereunder, at law or in equity including, without limitation, a decree of specific performance and/or injunctive relief with respect to the Maker’s failure to timely deliver Conversion Stock upon conversion of this Note as required pursuant to the terms hereof. 2 2.9 Restrictive Legend; Rule 144. Shares issued before they are eligible for resale under Rule 144 will bear a customary Securities Act restrictive legend. Once the shares are eligible for sale under Rule 144, the Maker will, at its expense and on the Holder’s request, obtain the legal opinion needed to remove the legend. 2.10 Transfer Taxes. The Maker pays any documentary stamp or similar taxes on issuance of the shares, except taxes arising from issuance in a name other than the Holder’s. 2.11 Share Reservation. The Maker will at all times reserve enough authorized and unissued shares of Common Stock to permit full conversion of this Note at the Conversion Price, including after any reverse split. 2.12 Dilution Acknowledged. The Maker’s obligation to issue shares on conversion is binding, regardless of the dilution to other shareholders. 2.13 Beneficial Ownership Limit. The Holder may not convert to the extent that, after conversion, the Holder and its affiliates would beneficially own more than 4.99% of the outstanding Common Stock, determined under Section 13(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Regulation 13D-G, which limitation may be increased on 61 days’ written notice from the Holder up to a maximum of 9.99% of the outstanding Common Stock. 2.14 Fundamental Transactions. If the Maker merges or consolidates with another Person, sells all or substantially all of its assets, completes a tender or exchange offer accepted by holders of more than 50% of the Common Stock, reclassifies or exchanges the Common Stock for other securities, cash or property, or enters a business combination in which another Person acquires more than 50% of its capital stock (each, a “ Fundamental Transaction ”), the Holder may, on conversion, receive the securities, cash and property it would have received had it converted immediately before (or after, whichever is greater) the Fundamental Transaction (the “ Alternate Consideration ”). Any successor entity must assume this Note in writing. Section 2.4 applies to any Fundamental Transaction that has the effect of a share combination. SECTION 3. EVENTS OF DEFAULT AND HOLDER REMEDIES 3.1 Events of Default. Each of the following is an “ Event of Default ”: (a) The Maker fails to pay principal or interest when due, whether at maturity or otherwise, and the failure continues for ten (10) business days after written notice from the Holder. (b) The Maker fails to deliver Conversion Stock by the Share Delivery Date, and the failure continues for five (5) business days after written notice from the Holder. (c) The Maker breaches any covenant in this Note or the Purchase Agreement, and the breach is not cured within thirty (30) days after written notice from the Holder. (d) The Maker breaches the covenants in Section 3.4 hereof, which breach shall not have any cure period. (e) The Maker applies for, or consents to, the appointment of a receiver, trustee or liquidator for itself or its property, which breach shall not have any cure period. (f) The Maker admits in writing its inability to pay its debts as they mature, or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, which breach shall not have any cure period. (g) The Maker files a voluntary bankruptcy petition, or a petition or answer seeking reorganization or an arrangement with creditors, which breach shall not have any cure period. (h) A court enters an order approving a bankruptcy petition filed against the Maker, and the order is not vacated, set aside or terminated within sixty (60) days. 3 (i) Any representation in this Note or in the Purchase Agreement proves materially false when made. (j) The Maker completes a Fundamental Transaction and the successor entity does not assume this Note in writing at the closing thereof. (k) The Maker fails to keep enough shares of Common Stock reserved under Section 2.11, above. (l) The Common Stock is delisted from the market on which it is listed or trading as of the Original Issue Date. (m) The Common Stock is no longer DWAC eligible. 3.2 Holder’s Election. After an Event of Default, and for so long as it continues, the Holder may, at its sole option, deliver a written notice in the form of Exhibit B (a “ Default Election Notice ”) choosing either remedy below. Until the Holder delivers a Default Election Notice, this Note stays outstanding under Remedy B. (a) Remedy A — Claw Back the Acquired Interest. The Maker will, within ten (10) business days after the Holder delivers a Default Election Notice choosing this Remedy A, transfer to the Holder the Clawback Interest, free and clear of all liens, claims and encumbrances, and deliver a signed assignment in the form of Exhibit C and any other documents the Target or the Holder reasonably requires. The “ Clawback Interest ” is the Acquired Interest multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is the “Credited Amount” [1] and the denominator of which is the original Principal Amount. In connection with this Remedy A and the reconveyance of the Clawback Interest, this Note shall be cancelled and deemed satisfied in full, including all accrued and unpaid interest and the Holder shall keep all interest previously paid and all shares of Conversion Stock previously issued, without the same being subject to any lien or other encumbrance. [2] The Holder need not refund any principal previously paid in cash. (b) Remedy B — Continue to Hold the Note. The Holder may keep this Note outstanding on its existing terms. Interest continues to accrue at 8% per annum, the conversion right under Section 2 continues at the $0.10 Conversion Price, and the Holder keeps its right to demand payment of all amounts then due. Choosing Remedy B does not waive the Event of Default. The Holder may later elect Remedy A by a new Default Election Notice, as long as an Event of Default is still continuing. 3.3 No Penalty. No default interest, late charge, premium, increased rate, liquidated damages or other penalty applies to the Maker because of an Event of Default. The Holder’s remedies are those in Section 3.2, together with its right to collect amounts due and its reasonable costs of collection and enforcement. Further, any payment made pursuant to Section 2.8 is compensation for an actual loss by the Holder and not a penalty. 3.4 Protection of the Acquired Interest. While any amount under this Note is outstanding, the Maker will not sell, transfer, pledge, encumber or grant any lien or option on the Acquired Interest, and will not vote it or take any action to dilute, redeem or materially impair it, without the Holder’s prior written consent. On the Original Issue Date, the Maker will deliver to an escrow agent an undated assignment of the Acquired Interest in the form of Exhibit C, signed in blank, to be released to the Holder only on exercise of Remedy A. 3.5 Remedies Cumulative. The Holder’s rights under this Note, the Purchase Agreement and applicable law are cumulative and may be exercised alternatively, successively or concurrently, except that the Holder may not both complete Remedy A and recover the cancelled amounts under this Note. [1] The “Credited Amount” is the total, as of the date of the Default Election Notice, of (i) all principal the Maker has paid in cash, (ii) all interest the Maker has paid in cash, and (iii) the Conversion Amount of every conversion the Holder has completed (the principal and interest converted, counted at the Conversion Price). [2] By way of example:, if the Credited Amount is $500,000, the Clawback Interest is 2.5% of the Target. If the Credited Amount is zero, the Clawback Interest is the full 5%. 4 SECTION 4. REPRESENTATIONS OF THE MAKER The Maker represents to the Holder that: (a) it is duly organized and in good standing under Nevada law; (b) it has authorized the issuance of this Note and the shares of Conversion Stock by all necessary corporate action; (c) this Note is its valid and binding obligation, enforceable under its terms; and (d) the shares of Conversion Stock, when issued under this Note, will be duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable. SECTION 5. MISCELLANEOUS 5.1 Transfers and Note Register. This Note may be transferred only in compliance with federal and state securities laws. The Maker may treat the person registered as the Holder on its note register as the owner for all purposes. 5.2 Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered personally, by e-mail, or by nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to the Maker go to GBT Technologies Inc., 21900 21900 Burbank Blvd, Attn: Chief Executive Officer, Minh@gbttechinc.com. Notices to the Holder go to MINDATORIUM INC., 9454 Wilshire Blvd, PH 37 Beverly Hills, CA 90212, Attn: Chief Executive Officer, ceo@mindatorium.com. A notice is effective on the earliest of: e-mail transmission before 5:00 p.m. recipient’s time on a business day (otherwise the next business day); the second business day after deposit with an overnight courier; or actual receipt. 5.3 Waivers by the Maker. The Maker waives demand, presentment, protest and notice of any kind, and consents to extensions of time for payment and other indulgences, all without notice. 5.4 Amendments. This Note may be amended, waived or terminated only by a written agreement signed by the Maker and the Holder. 5.5 Lost or Mutilated Note. If this Note is lost, stolen, destroyed or mutilated, the Maker will issue a replacement Note on receipt of reasonably satisfactory evidence of the loss and of ownership. 5.6 Governing Law and Venue. This Note is governed by the internal laws of the State of California, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in Los Angeles County, California, and waive any objection to venue there. 5.7 Attorneys’ Fees. In any action to enforce this Note, the prevailing party recovers its reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs. 5.8 Severability. If any provision is held invalid, illegal or unenforceable, the remaining provisions stay in full effect. 5.9 Successors and Assigns. This Note binds the Maker and its successors and benefits the Holder and its successors, endorsees and assigns. 5.10 Headings. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. text: EX-10.36 4 e8044_ex10-36.htm EXHIBIT 10.36 EXHIBIT 10.36 EXECUTIVE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT THIS EXECUTIVE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT (this “ Agreement ”) is made and entered effective as of October 5, 2026 (“Effective Date”), between GBT Technologies, Inc., a Nevada corporation, (the “ Company ”), and Richard L. Taw, III, an individual (the “ Executive ”). RECITALS: A. The Company is a Technology Company (the “Business”). B. Executive wishes to work for the Company and the Company wishes to employ Executive pursuant to the terms and provisions of this Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual agreements herein made, the Company and the Executive hereby agree as follows: 1. Employment. The Company hereby agrees to employ Executive as Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) of GBT Technologies, and Executive hereby accepts such employment, upon the terms and conditions hereinafter set forth. During the “Term” (including any renewals thereof), as defined herein, Executive’s duties and responsibilities shall be duties generally performed by the Chief Marketing Officer of a company with a similar business. Executive shall report to the President of the Company. Executive shall devote the time and effort necessary to perform his duties to the Company, provided, however, that Executive shall not be prevented from serving as an officer or director in other companies, or investing his personal assets or personal time in investments or business entities, as hereinafter defined. 2. Compensation/Benefits. a. Salary. Company shall pay Executive a base salary of Twenty Thousand Dollars ($20,000) per month during the Term, payable in cash or in shares of the Company’s common stock of equivalent value as provided below. The form of payment (cash, shares, or a combination thereof) shall be determined by the Board of Directors, and the parties intend to transition to cash payment as the Company’s cash position permits. Any shares issued in payment of salary shall be issued at a price of $0.00005 per share (adjusted for stock splits, reverse splits and similar recapitalizations) and shall be deemed earned on the 1st day of each applicable month. The Company shall issue such shares within ten (10) business days after the end of the month in which they are earned and shall bear the cost of any legal opinions and transfer agent fees associated with the issuance of such shares and the removal of restrictive legends when permitted by applicable law. b. Employee Benefits. The Executive shall be entitled to participate in all benefit programs of the Company currently existing or hereafter made available by the Board of Directors to other executive employees, including, but not limited to, pension and other retirement plans, including any 401K Plan, group life insurance, dental, hospitalization, surgical and major medical coverage, sick leave, salary continuation, vacation and holidays, long-term disability and other benefits. c. Vacation. The Executive shall be entitled to Two (2) weeks of paid vacation during each twelve (12) month period of the Term in addition to standard legal holidays. d. Business Expense Reimbursement. The Executive shall be entitled to receive reimbursement for reasonable, out-of-pocket expenses incurred in accordance with Company policies established by the Board of Directors and Executive shall provide appropriate written documentation evidencing such expenses so as to enable the Company to deduct them for federal income tax purposes. 3. Term. The Term of employment hereunder will commence as of the Effective Date and end Thirty Six (36) months from the Effective Date (“Term”), unless terminated pursuant to Section 4 of this Agreement. 4. Death, Disability and Termination. a. Death. In the event of the death of the Executive during the Term of the Agreement, salary shall be paid to the Executive’s designated beneficiary, or, in the absence of such designation, to the estate or other legal representative of the Executive. The Company shall also pay to the Executive’s estate or heirs, as the case may be, any accrued and unpaid compensation. b. Termination by the Company for Cause. (i) Nothing herein shall prevent the Company from terminating the Executive’s employment for “Cause” as hereinafter defined. Any rights and benefits the Executive may have in respect of any other compensation shall be determined in accordance with the terms of such other compensation arrangements or such plans or programs. (ii) “Cause” shall mean (a) committing or participating in an injurious act of fraud, gross neglect, misrepresentation, embezzlement or dishonesty against the Company; (b) committing or participating in any other injurious act or omission wantonly, willfully, recklessly or in a manner which was grossly negligent against the Company (monetarily or otherwise); (c) engaging in a criminal enterprise involving moral turpitude; (d) conviction of an act or acts constituting a felony under the laws of the United States or any state thereof, (e) Executive’s failure to substantially perform his material duties hereunder or to substantially comply with any other material provision of this Agreement, (f) a willful act by Executive as a result of which he knowingly receives an improper material personal benefit at the expense of the Company, (g) any other willful misconduct by Executive that is materially injurious to the business or business reputation of the Company, or (h) any other circumstance which constitutes “cause” under applicable law. (iii) Notwithstanding anything else contained in this Agreement, this Agreement will not be deemed to have been terminated for Cause unless and until there shall have been delivered to the Executive a notice of termination from the Board of Directors of the Company stating that the Executive committed one of the types of conduct set forth in Section 4(b)(ii) of this Agreement and specifying the particulars thereof and the Executive shall be given a Ten (10) day period to cure such conduct set forth in Section 4(b)(ii). c. Voluntary Termination. Either the Executive or the Company may terminate the Executive’s employment prior to the expiration of the Term, including any renewals thereof, for any reason other than Cause, by giving the other party not less than thirty (30) days’ prior written notice. Such termination shall constitute a voluntary termination and in such event the Executive shall receive base salary only for the period ending with the date of such termination, which shall be no earlier than the end of the thirty (30) day notice period. If the Company elects to end the Executive’s services before the end of the notice period, base salary shall continue through the end of the notice period. All base salary earned through the termination date, including any shares of the Company’s common stock earned under Section 2(a), shall be paid or issued to the Executive within ten (10) business days after the termination date on the terms set forth in Section 2(a). Any rights and benefits the Executive may have in respect of any other compensation shall be determined in accordance with the terms of such other compensation arrangements or such plans or programs. 5. Covenant Not to Compete. Executive acknowledges and recognizes the highly competitive nature of Company’s business and the goodwill and business strategy of the Company and continued patronage constitute a substantial asset of the Company. The Executive recognizes that the terms of this covenant are reasonable and necessary for the protection of the Company’s business because the value of Executive’s services will be enhanced by his association with the Company. Accordingly, Executive agrees to the following: a. That during the Term (the “Restricted Period”), Executive will not, indirectly or directly, compete with the Company by soliciting, inducing or influencing any of the Company’s customers or employees at any time during the Restricted Period to discontinue or reduce the extent of such relationship with the Company. b. The provision of this Section 5 will not be in effect for any corporation or partnership the Company is a direct or indirect shareholder or interest holder, and/or has entered into any kind of joint venture relationship or partnership with the Company. 6. Non-Disclosure of Confidential Information. a. Executive acknowledges that the Company’s trade secrets, private or secret processes, methods and ideas as they exist from time to time, information concerning the Company’s products, business records and plans, inventions, acquisition strategy, price structure and pricing, discounts, costs, computer programs and listings, source code and/or subject code, copyright trademark proprietary information, formulae, protocols, forms, procedures, training methods, development technical information, know-how, show-how, new product and service development, advertising budgets, past, present and future marketing, activities and procedures, method for operating the Company’s Business, credit and financial data concerning the Company’s Clients and customer lists, which customer lists shall not only mean one or more of the names and address of the customers of the Company, but it shall also encompass any and all information whatsoever regarding them, including their needs, and marketing; advertising, promotional and sales strategies, sales presentations, research information, revenues, acquisitions, practices and plans and information which is embodied in written or otherwise recorded form, and other information of a confidential nature not known publicly or by other companies selling to the same markets and specifically including information which is mental, not physical (collectively, the “Confidential Information”), are valuable, special and unique assets of the Company, access to and knowledge of which have been provided to Executive by virtue of Executive’s association with the Company. In light of the highly competitive nature of the industry in which the Company’s business is conducted, Executive agrees that all Confidential Information, heretofore or in the future obtained by Executive as a result of Executive’s association with the Company shall be considered confidential. b. The Executive agrees that the Executive shall (i) hold in confidence and not disclose or make available to any third party any such Confidential Information obtained directly or constructively from the Company, unless so authorized in writing by the Company; (ii) exercise all reasonable efforts to prevent third parties from gaining access to the Confidential Information; (iii) not use, directly or indirectly the Confidential Information except in order to perform the Executive’s duties and responsibilities to the Company; (iv) restrict the disclosure or availability of the Confidential Information to those who have agreed to maintain the confidentiality of the Confidential Information and who have a need to know the information in order to achieve the purposes of this Agreement; (v) not copy or modify any Confidential Information without prior written consent of the Company, provided, however, that such copy or modification of any Confidential Information does not include any modifications or copying which would otherwise prevent the Executive from performing his/her duties and responsibilities to the Company; (vi) take such other protective measures as may be reasonably necessary to preserve the confidentiality of the Confidential Information; (vii) relinquish all rights Executive may have in any matter, such as drawings, documents, models, samples, photographs, patterns, templates, molds, tools or prototypes, which may contain, embody or make use of the Confidential Information; and (viii) promptly deliver to the Company any such matter as the Company may direct at any time, and not retain any copies or other reproductions thereof. c. Upon written request of the Company, Executive shall return to the Company all written materials containing the Confidential Information. Executive shall also deliver to the Company written statements signed by Executive certifying that all materials have been returned within five (5) days of receipt of the request. 7. Indemnification by the Company. The Company shall, to the maximum extent permitted by law, indemnify, defend and hold Executive harmless for any acts or decisions made in good faith while performing services for the Company. To the same extent, the Company shall pay, and subject to any legal limitations, advance all expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees incurred by Executive in connection with the defense of any action, suit or proceeding and in connection with any appeal, which has been brought against Executive by reason of his service as an officer or agent of the Company. If and when the Company obtains directors’ and officers’ liability insurance, the Executive shall be covered under such policy as an insured officer on terms no less favorable than those provided to the Company’s other officers and directors. 8. Amendments. This Agreement shall not be modified or amended except by written agreement duly executed by the parties hereto. 9. Headings. All sections and descriptive headings of this Agreement are inserted for convenience only, and shall not affect the construction or interpretation hereof. 10. Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which, when executed and delivered, shall be an original, but all counterparts shall together constitute one and the same instrument. 11. Entire Agreement. This Agreement hereto constitutes the entire understanding between the parties. Nothing in this Agreement will prevent or restrict Executive from serving on the Board of Directors of public or private companies and receive compensation from such service. 12. Governing Law. This Agreement is to be construed and enforced according to the laws of the State of California. This Agreement shall not be construed more strictly against one party than the other, merely by virtue of the fact that it may have been prepared by counsel for one of the parties, it being recognized that both Company and Executive have contributed substantially and materially to the negotiation and preparation of this Agreement. 13. Venue. Venue in any action arising from this Agreement shall be in Los Angeles or Orange County, California. 14. Attorneys’ Fees. In connection with any controversy arising out of this Agreement, the prevailing party shall be entitled to reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs at pretrial, trial, and appellate levels from the non-prevailing party. 15. Severability. Inapplicability or unenforceability of any provision of this Agreement shall not limit or impair the operation or validity of any other provision of this Agreement or any such other instrument. 16. Non-Assignability. This Agreement is personal in nature and not assignable by any party hereto. 17. Binding Effect. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties, their respective successors, transferees and assigns. 18. Construction. In construing this Agreement, the singular shall include the plural and the plural shall include the singular, and the use of any gender shall include every other and all genders. 19. Relationship and Covenants of Executive. Executive acknowledges that the relationship between the parties hereto is exclusively that of Company and employee. The Company shall be the sole owner of all the fruits and proceeds of Executive’s services hereunder, including, but not limited to, all ideas, concepts, formats, software designs, suggestions, developments, arrangements, articles, stories, writings, compilations, campaigns, packages, programs, promotions and other intellectual properties which Executive may create in connection with Executive’s activities as an employee of the Company during the Term (“Executive’s Work Product”), free and clear of any and all claims by Executive (or anyone claiming under or through Executive). Executive is rendering his services hereunder as an employee-for-hire by the Company and that all such writings and materials developed by Executive in connection with the Company’s business are work-made-for-hire under the copyright law of the United States. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the ownership provisions of this Section 19 apply only to work the Executive performs for the Company, including its Cube X Media brand. Executive’s Work Product does not include, and the Company shall acquire no right, title or interest in, the Executive’s separate business ventures listed on Exhibit A (the “Excluded Ventures”) or any intellectual property owned, developed or used by the Excluded Ventures, whether before or after the Effective Date, provided such intellectual property is not developed using the Company’s Confidential Information or as part of the Executive’s services to the Company. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first above written in Los Angeles, California. THE COMPANY By: Name: Minh Collins Its: CEO & Director EXECUTIVE Richard L. Taw, III

text: EX-10.1 2 d189549dex101.htm EX-10.1 EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 November 4, 2026 DELIVERED TO: Matthew Goldberg RE: Separation Agreement and General Release Dear Matt: This Separation Agreement and General Release (the “ Agreement ”) sets forth the understanding between you, Matthew Goldberg, and Tripadvisor, Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ Tripadvisor ”), and Tripadvisor LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“ Tripadvisor LLC ” and, together with Tripadvisor, the “ Company ”), concerning the conclusion of your employment and an orderly leadership transition. The purpose of this Agreement is to establish an amicable arrangement for ending your employment relationship, to release legally waivable claims, and to provide the separation payments and benefits described below. Your “ Employment Agreement ” is your May 2, 2022 Employment Letter Agreement with Tripadvisor LLC. The “ ESP ” is the Tripadvisor, Inc. Amended and Restated Executive Severance Plan and Summary Plan Description. The “ Participation Letter ” is the August 6, 2025 letter agreement between you and Tripadvisor concerning your participation in the ESP as CEO. You have at least twenty-one (21) calendar days after receiving this Agreement to consider whether to sign it. To accept, deliver a signed copy via DocuSign or to the General Counsel, Tripadvisor LLC, 400 1st Avenue, Needham, MA 02494, within twenty-one (21) calendar days after receipt. You may revoke your acceptance as described in Section 5. This Agreement becomes effective on the eighth calendar day after you sign it, provided the Company has signed it and you have not timely revoked it (the “ Agreement Effective Date ”). The Section 2 payments and benefits also require your execution and nonrevocation, following separation, of the Supplemental Release attached as Exhibit A. 1. Employment Status, Transition, Final Payments and Termination of Benefits a. Separation and transition. Your employment with the Company will end no later than February 16, 2027 (the “ Scheduled Separation Date ”). You are expected to remain employed through the Scheduled Separation Date, support an orderly transition, and perform duties reasonably assigned by Tripadvisor’s Board of Directors (the “ Board ”) consistent with that transition. The date your employment actually ends is the “ Separation Date .” During your continued employment, your base salary, employee benefits, and ordinary-course equity vesting will continue in accordance with the applicable arrangements, except as expressly modified here. If the Company elects to end your employment before the Scheduled Separation Date for any reason other than for Cause, you will remain entitled to all compensation, payments, and benefits described in this Section 1 and Section 2, subject to the release and other conditions expressly stated in this Agreement. Cause has the meaning in paragraph 11(b)(vi) of the Employment Agreement, including applicable notice and cure requirements. If you elect to resign for any reason before the Scheduled Separation Date, you will not be entitled to any compensation, payments, or benefits described in Section 2. b. Consent to specified transition changes. You and the Company agree that any agreed-to changes to your position or responsibilities during the transition period will not constitute Good Reason under the Employment Agreement, ESP, any Participation Letter, or any equity award agreement, or give rise to additional severance. c. Resignations. Effective as of the Separation Date or any earlier date requested by the Board, you hereby resign from the Board and all officer, director, employee, committee, fiduciary and other positions you hold with the Company and its subsidiaries and affiliates, and any other position. You will deliver signed resignation instruments and reasonably assist with related filings and transition formalities. No such requested resignation shall impact your substantive rights under this Agreement. d. Accrued obligations. Whether or not you sign or revoke this Agreement or Exhibit A, the Company will pay your accrued and earned but unpaid base salary and accrued but unused vacation through the Separation Date, and all vested and accrued benefits (the “ Accrued Obligations ”). Salary and vacation will be paid within the time required by applicable law. The Company will also reimburse properly documented business expenses incurred through the Separation Date in accordance with the Employment Agreement and Company policy. e. Benefits and COBRA. Active employment compensation and benefit participation will end on the Separation Date or such later date as the applicable plan requires, except as expressly provided here or required by law. You will cease accruing vacation and additional benefits after employment ends. Vested benefits remain governed by the applicable plans. You and your eligible dependents will receive separate information concerning COBRA continuation coverage. A timely election must be made within the applicable statutory period, generally sixty (60) days after the later of the election notice and loss of coverage; timely elected coverage will be retroactive as required by law. 2. Separation Pay and Other Benefits Subject to the effective release in this Agreement and Exhibit A, and the other conditions below, you and the Company agree on each of the payments, benefits, and other terms set forth below. These payments, benefits, and other terms replace, and are not in addition to, separation-related payments, benefits, and equity-vesting entitlements under the Employment Agreement, ESP, Participation Letter, and equity award agreements. No duplicate or additional severance is payable under those arrangements for this separation. The Company’s obligations under this Section are conditioned on the Agreement Effective Date occurring, your remaining employed through the Scheduled Separation Date unless the Company elects to end your employment earlier as contemplated by Section 1(a), your timely execution and delivery of Exhibit A, in form provided to you by the Company, on or after the Separation Date and its becoming irrevocable no later than sixty (60) days after the Separation Date, your return of Company property under Section 3, and compliance with the continuing obligations 2 under Section 7(c). If you elect to resign for any reason before the Scheduled Separation Date, no payments or benefits under this Section are payable. The date Exhibit A becomes effective and irrevocable is the “ Release Effective Date .” You must deliver an executed Exhibit A within twenty-one (21) calendar days after the later of your receipt of a completed Exhibit A from the Company and the Separation Date. a. Salary severance. The Company will pay an amount equal to nine (9) months of your annual base salary rate in effect on the Separation Date, less required withholdings. This aggregate amount is $675,000. Payment will be made as salary continuation over the eighteen (18)-month period beginning the day after the Separation Date, on regular payroll dates. Payments will begin on the first practicable regular payroll date after the Release Effective Date, no later than sixty (60) days after the Separation Date, subject to Section 8(g). The first payment will include a catch-up for installments that otherwise would have been paid since separation. If that sixty (60)-day period spans two calendar years, payments will commence in the second year. b. Bonus severance. The Company will pay a lump sum equal to $675,000, which is 0.75 times your annual Target Bonus in effect for the year in which the Separation Date occurs, less required withholdings, on the first practicable payroll date after the Release Effective Date, subject to Section 8(g). “ Target Bonus ” means your annual target bonus opportunity in effect for that year, not a prorated amount. c. Health care continuation. If you participate in the Company’s group health plans immediately before separation, timely elect COBRA, and remain eligible, the Company will pay the full amount of the COBRA premium for continuation of the coverage maintained by you and your eligible dependents immediately before separation, including applicable medical, dental, and vision coverage. The subsidy will begin upon commencement of COBRA coverage and end on the earlier of eighteen (18) months after the Separation Date and the date you become ineligible for COBRA under COBRA or the related regulations. You must immediately notify the Company of loss of eligibility. After the subsidy ends, coverage may continue as permitted by law and the plans, at your full expense. No cash is payable in lieu of unused coverage. d. Annual bonus treatment. You will not be eligible for any annual bonus from with respect to calendar years 2026 or 2027, whether in full or pro rata. This exclusion does not reduce the bonus severance expressly payable under Section 2(b). e. Equity vesting. For each equity award held by you that is outstanding and unvested on the Separation Date, the Company will first determine the portion that would vest upon a Qualifying Termination outside the Change in Control Period under the Participation Letter, without applying the fifty percent (50%) reduction described below. That determination will include all portions that would, but for termination of employment, have vested during the eighteen (18) months following the Separation Date (the “ Equity Acceleration Period ”). If an award’s vesting schedule would result in a smaller percentage (or none) of the award being vested through the end of the Equity Acceleration Period than if it vested annually pro rata over its vesting period, the award will be treated as though it vested annually pro rata over its vesting period for this 3 determination. If an award specifies a more favorable post-termination vesting schedule, that schedule will instead govern the determination for that award. Fifty percent (50%) of the resulting eligible unvested portion of each equity award, and not fifty percent (50%) of all outstanding unvested awards without regard to eligibility, will vest on the later of the Separation Date and Release Effective Date, except to the extent the applicable more favorable award-specific schedule or unsatisfied performance conditions provide for later vesting. No portion will be counted twice. Any otherwise eligible portion for which a performance condition has not been satisfied will remain outstanding solely for determination of the applicable performance condition(s) and vest only if, and when, such condition(s) is satisfied under the applicable award terms. Performance conditions, including those applicable to performance-based restricted stock units, are not deemed achieved by this Agreement. Except for portions preserved by this paragraph and vested awards, remaining unvested portions will be forfeited on the Separation Date. Settlement will occur upon vesting to the extent permitted by Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (“ Section 409 ”); an existing settlement schedule will govern to the extent required for Section 409A compliance. Except as expressly modified here, the equity plans and award agreements remain in effect. As reflected in the Company’s records as of the date of this Agreement, you hold (1) 222,416 RSUs that are scheduled to vest during such 18-month period, (2) 44,410 PSUs from the 2025 grant, as to which applicable performance period has been completed and actual payout will be determined in ordinary course in 2027, and (3) 101,085 PSUs (at target performance levels) as to which the applicable performance period has not been completed. f. Option and stock appreciation right exercise period. All vested stock options and stock appreciation rights held by you as of the Separation Date, including those that vest pursuant to Section 2(e), will remain exercisable through their respective originally scheduled expiration dates, subject to Section 409A. No award will be exercisable before it vests, and no award’s originally scheduled expiration date will be extended. As reflected in the Company’s records as of the date of this Agreement, you hold 515,808 options, all of which are vested. g. Mitigation and offset. Consistent with the Participation Letter, the first sentence of Section 10.1 of the ESP does not apply to you: you have no obligation to seek other employment or take other actions to mitigate the amounts payable under this Agreement. The remaining provisions of Section 10.1 of the ESP remain applicable to separation payments and benefits under this Agreement. Accordingly, the Company retains its right to offset earnings from another employer during that period against Severance Benefits as provided in Section 10.1 of the ESP, and you remain subject to its employment-status reporting and periodic certification requirements and its related withholding and recovery provisions. With respect to the foregoing, earnings subject to the offset shall mean earnings as a common law employee, not via service on a Board of Directors or similar. 4 h. Conditions; death after separation. Section 3.3 of the ESP concerning restrictive-covenant compliance, conduct constituting Cause, and related remedies continues to apply except as expressly modified here. These incorporated provisions do not permit denial of Section 2 payments or benefits solely because the Company elects to terminate your employment before the Scheduled Separation Date, or forfeiture of Accrued Obligations, interference with protected activity under Section 7(b), or denial of rights preserved by Section 4(c). If you die after separation and after executing an unrevoked Exhibit A, remaining cash separation benefits will be paid to your estate under Section 3.4 of the ESP, subject to Section 8(g); equity and surviving dependents’ statutory health coverage rights remain governed by their applicable arrangements as modified here. 3. Return of Property The Company will permit you to retain your Company-issued laptop and iPad, provided you first cooperate with the Company to wipe such devices of all Company-related information. Other than as expressly permitted herein, on or before the Separation Date, you will return all Company confidential and proprietary information and other property, including documents, notes, customer lists and copies, corporate cards, access cards, keys, office equipment, phones, and storage devices, and will not retain Company information in personal accounts or devices. You will reasonably cooperate in identifying and securely returning or deleting such information, subject to legal preservation obligations. You may retain personal compensation and benefits records, agreements governing your rights, and information lawfully retained to exercise preserved rights, subject to applicable confidentiality obligations. Nothing requires destruction of evidence or restricts Section 7(a) activity. 4. Release a. General release. In consideration of the Company’s undertakings, you, on behalf of yourself and your heirs, representatives, administrators and executors, voluntarily, irrevocably and unconditionally release the Released Parties defined in Section 6 from all legally waivable complaints, claims, demands, contracts, liabilities, actions, causes of action, promises and rights, known or unknown, in law or equity, that you now own or hold or have ever owned or held, arising from acts, omissions, transactions, or occurrences on or before the date you sign this Agreement, including those connected with your employment, compensation, officer or director service, or separation. This includes legally waivable claims under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964; the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 (“ ADEA ”); the Americans with Disabilities Act; the Equal Pay Act; the National Labor Relations Act; the Family and Medical Leave Act; the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act; the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974; the Massachusetts Fair Employment Practices Law, Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 151B; the Massachusetts Payment of Wages Act, Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 149, Sections 148 and 150; the Fair Labor Standards Act, only to the extent lawfully waivable; the Massachusetts Earned Sick Time law; the Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave law; the Massachusetts Wage Act, M.G.L. c. 149, §§148-150C; the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination; the New Jersey Conscientious Employee Protection Act; the New Jersey Family Leave Act; the New Jersey Wage Payment Law; the New Jersey Wage and Hour Law; the New Jersey Equal Pay Act; the New Jersey WARN Act, N.J. Stat. Ann. § 34:21-1 et seq,; the New Jersey Paid Sick Leave Act; the New York State Human Rights Law; the New York Labor Law (including but not limited to the New York State Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act; all provisions prohibiting discrimination and retaliation, and 5 all provisions regulating wage and hour law); the New York State Correction Law; the New York State Civil Rights Law; Section 125 of the New York Workers’ Compensation Law; the New York City Human Rights Law; the New York Wage Theft Prevention Act; the New York Wage Payment Act; the New York Equal Pay Law; the Diane B. Allen Equal Pay Act; retaliation claims under the New Jersey Workers’ Compensation Law; and other applicable federal, state, and local employment, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, and wage laws, as amended. It also includes legally waivable contract, promissory estoppel, tort, misrepresentation, libel, slander, fraud, compensation, bonus, severance, equity, securities-law, and attorneys’ fee claims. b. Known and unknown claims; settlement. Subject to Section 4(c), this release covers known and unknown claims existing through your signature date, even if you later discover different facts. Subject to the Company’s performance and preserved rights, Sections 1 and 2 fully settle the Company’s compensation and separation obligations arising from this separation. Signing this Agreement does not release later-arising claims; Exhibit A separately covers claims through its signature date. c. Excluded claims and preserved rights. Neither this Agreement nor Exhibit A releases: rights that cannot lawfully be released by private agreement; claims arising after the applicable release signature date; rights to enforce this Agreement; Accrued Obligations, vested and accrued benefits, and vested equity rights under applicable arrangements as expressly modified here; unemployment or workers’ compensation benefits; rights to indemnification, advancement, contribution, or directors’ and officers’ liability insurance under paragraph 12 of the Employment Agreement, organizational documents, agreements, policies, or law; or Section 7(a) rights. 5. Waiver of ADEA Rights and Claims; Consideration and Revocation You specifically and voluntarily waive legally waivable ADEA rights and claims arising on or before your signature date, but not thereafter. The promises and benefits exchanged for the releases and negotiated resolution of separation entitlements constitute good and valuable consideration beyond that to which you would be entitled without satisfying the applicable release conditions. You are advised in writing to consult an attorney before signing this Agreement or Exhibit A. You have at least twenty-one (21) calendar days after receipt to consider this Agreement and may voluntarily sign sooner. You will separately have at least twenty-one (21) calendar days to consider Exhibit A, which you may not sign before separation. You acknowledge that you understand the terms, have had the opportunity to obtain advice, and act knowingly and voluntarily without improper influence. The parties agree that revisions do not restart the consideration period to the extent permitted by law. You may revoke this Agreement within seven (7) calendar days after signing by written notice actually received within that period by the General Counsel, Tripadvisor LLC, 400 1st Avenue, Needham, MA 02494. This Agreement is not effective or enforceable before the Agreement Effective Date. Timely revocation means no separation benefits are payable under this Agreement. Exhibit A has its own seven (7)-day revocation period; revoking it does not rescind an otherwise effective Agreement but prevents entitlement to release-conditioned benefits. 6 6. Construction For Sections 4 and 5 and Exhibit A, “ Released Parties ” means Tripadvisor, Tripadvisor LLC, each of their affiliated and related entities, their respective predecessors, successors, and assigns, their respective employee benefit plans and fiduciaries of such plans, and the current and former officers, directors, shareholders, employees, attorneys, accountants, and agents of each of the foregoing in their official and personal capacities. 7. Future Conduct a. Protected rights and disclosures. Nothing here, in Exhibit A or in any continuing obligation restricts filing charges or complaints with, communicating directly with, providing information or documents to, or participating or cooperating in investigations or proceedings of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Securities and Exchange Commission, Department of Justice, Department of Labor, National Labor Relations Board, Congress, an Inspector General, or other governmental authority; reporting suspected violations; making legally protected disclosures; truthful testimony; discussing or disclosing discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or other conduct to the extent protected by law; or exercising applicable National Labor Relations Act Section 7 rights. You need no Company authorization and need not notify the Company. Nothing waives any governmental whistleblower award or other nonwaivable payment. To the extent lawful, you waive individual monetary relief for released claims, but not governmental awards or nonwaivable relief. Under 18 U.S.C. Section 1833(b), you will not be criminally or civilly liable under federal or state trade secret law for disclosure of a trade secret made in confidence to a governmental official, directly or indirectly, or an attorney, solely to report or investigate a suspected violation of law, or in a complaint or document filed under seal in a proceeding. In a retaliation action for reporting a suspected violation, you may disclose the trade secret to counsel and use it in the proceeding if you file any document containing it under seal and otherwise disclose it only by court order. All confidentiality, notice, cooperation, non-disparagement, and remedy provisions are subject to this Section 7(a). b. Cooperation. At reasonable times and places not unreasonably interfering with your then professional obligations, you will reasonably assist the Company and counsel in proceedings, investigations, and matters relating to your services, provide truthful information, and execute reasonably necessary documents. The Company will reimburse reasonable documented expenses. If the time required of you under this subsection 7(b) is more than de minimis , the Company and you agree to discuss in good faith, with the agreed-upon goal of aligning on reasonable compensation for your time. Except where prohibited by law or inconsistent with Section 7(a), you will promptly notify the General Counsel of subpoenas or court orders seeking Company confidential information and allow reasonable opportunity to seek protection. Section 7(a) activity requires no advance notice, disclosure of communications, or approval. You need not waive privilege or act contrary to law. 7 c. Continuing obligations. You reaffirm, without expanding or restarting, continuing obligations under the Non-Disclosure, Developments and Non-Competition Agreement executed in connection with your Employment Agreement (the “ Restrictive Covenant Agreement ”) and other existing confidentiality, intellectual property, and restrictive-covenant obligations, according to their terms and to the extent legally enforceable. 8. Representations and Miscellaneous Provisions a. Entire agreement; priority. Neither party has relied on outside promises or representations. This Agreement and Exhibit A contain the complete understanding concerning this separation and supersede the term sheet and prior understandings on that subject. The Employment Agreement, ESP, Participation Letter, and equity award agreements remain operative only to the extent not expressly modified or superseded here, including preserved vested and accrued rights, indemnification, applicable tax provisions, and continuing obligations. For this separation, this Agreement controls over conflicting separation entitlements, notwithstanding another arrangement’s more-favorable-treatment or no-reduction provision, and you expressly agree to these negotiated reductions. b. Severability and construction. An unenforceable provision will be severed or limited as permitted by law without invalidating the remainder. Release enforceability will be resolved under applicable law without expanding released claims or impairing nonwaivable rights. This Agreement will be construed as a whole according to its fair meaning, not strictly for or against either party. c. Authority; successors. You have capacity and authority to enter this Agreement and have not assigned released claims. Each Company signatory represents that the signatory is authorized and necessary approvals to enter and perform this Agreement have been obtained. This binds you and your heirs, representatives, administrators, and executors and the Company and its successors and assigns. You may not assign except by will or descent and distribution. A permitted Company assignment will not relieve the Company of its obligations. d. Governing law; forum; jury waiver. This Agreement shall be governed by Massachusetts law without regard to conflicts principles. Subject to nonwaivable rights, enforcement claims shall be brought in a competent Massachusetts court, and the parties consent to jurisdiction and venue there. TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, EACH PARTY KNOWINGLY AND VOLUNTARILY WAIVES TRIAL BY JURY IN A DISPUTE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT. e. No admission. This Agreement and its execution are not an admission by you or the Company of liability, wrongdoing, violation, error or omission. f. Withholding and tax responsibility. Payments and benefits are subject to required withholding. The Company makes no representation about personal tax consequences. You are responsible for taxes imposed on you, without relieving the Company of its own withholding or tax obligations. 8 g. Section 409A. This Agreement is intended to be exempt from or comply with Section 409A. Each installment is a separate payment. A termination-triggered payment subject to Section 409A requires a separation from service within its meaning. If you are a specified employee, amounts subject to the required six-month delay will be paid on the first business day after the earlier of six (6) months following separation from service and death; delayed amounts will be paid then in a lump sum without interest, and remaining amounts on their original schedule. If a release-conditioned payment period spans two (2) calendar years, a Section 409A payment will be made in the second year; you may not select its taxable year. Reimbursements must be made by the last day of the year following the expense year; amounts available in one year will not affect another except as permitted for medical expenses; and reimbursement and in-kind rights cannot be exchanged for other benefits. Payment and equity settlement dates may not be accelerated or deferred except as permitted by Section 409A. Release timing will not change a payment date required to be retained under an existing deferred compensation arrangement. h. Counterparts and electronic signatures. This Agreement and Exhibit A may be signed in counterparts, each an original and together one instrument. Electronic signatures and delivery by DocuSign, PDF or comparable means are effective as originals. If you agree to the foregoing, please sign and return this Agreement as described above. Very truly yours, TRIPADVISOR, INC. By: /s/ Bradford Young Name: Bradford Young Title: General Counsel Date: November 4, 2026 TRIPADVISOR LLC By: /s/ Bradford Young Name: Bradford Young Title: General Counsel Date: November 4, 2026 9 I HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THIS AGREEMENT, HAVE BEEN ADVISED TO CONSULT AN ATTORNEY AND HAVE HAD SUFFICIENT TIME TO DO SO, AND AM KNOWINGLY AND VOLUNTARILY SIGNING IT. Agreed and accepted: /s/ Matthew Goldberg Matthew Goldberg Date: November 4, 2026 10 EXHIBIT A SUPPLEMENTAL RELEASE DO NOT SIGN BEFORE THE SEPARATION DATE. This Supplemental Release is given by Matthew Goldberg (“ you ”) under the Separation Agreement and General Release between you, Tripadvisor, Inc. and Tripadvisor LLC dated [•] (the “ Agreement ”). Undefined capitalized terms have the Agreement’s meanings. Your Separation Date is [insert actual date employment ended, no later than February 16, 2027]. In consideration of the Section 2 payments and benefits, which require this Supplemental Release to become effective and irrevocable, you reaffirm and repeat the Section 4 release and Section 5 ADEA waiver, incorporated here as though fully set forth, covering all legally waivable claims against the Released Parties arising from acts, omissions, transactions or occurrences on or before the date you sign this Supplemental Release, including your employment and its termination. You specifically waive claims under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 arising on or before this signature date, but not later-arising claims. All exclusions and preserved rights under Section 4(c) and protected rights and disclosures under Section 7(a) apply here. This Supplemental Release does not waive enforcement of the Agreement, Accrued Obligations, vested and accrued benefits, equity rights preserved by the Agreement, indemnification, advancement, contribution, directors’ and officers’ liability insurance, nonwaivable rights, or governmental whistleblower awards. No penalty or tender-back obligation applies to challenging an ADEA waiver. You reaffirm your continuing obligations and confirm return of Company property as required by Section 3, subject to its exceptions. Your employment ended on the Separation Date in accordance with Section 1(a), and you confirm your Section 1(c) resignations. This Supplemental Release creates no new noncompetition obligation. You are advised in writing to consult an attorney before signing. You have at least twenty-one (21) calendar days after the later of receipt and the Separation Date to consider this Supplemental Release. You may knowingly and voluntarily sign sooner, but not before the Separation Date. To receive Section 2 benefits, deliver it in the manner specified for the Agreement within that twenty-one-day period and sufficiently early that it becomes irrevocable within sixty (60) days after the Separation Date. The Company’s undertakings and Section 2 benefits constitute good and valuable consideration. You may revoke this Supplemental Release within seven (7) calendar days after signing by written notice actually received within that period by the General Counsel, Tripadvisor LLC, 400 1st Avenue, Needham, MA 02494. This Supplemental Release becomes effective on the eighth calendar day after signature, provided you have not timely revoked it (the “ Release Effective Date ”), and is not enforceable before then. Revocation prevents entitlement to Section 2 benefits but does not revoke an otherwise effective Agreement or affect Accrued Obligations or nonwaivable rights. The Agreement’s interpretation, governing-law, and counterpart provisions apply. 11 I HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THIS SUPPLEMENTAL RELEASE, HAVE BEEN ADVISED TO CONSULT AN ATTORNEY, HAVE BEEN GIVEN AT LEAST TWENTY-ONE DAYS TO CONSIDER IT, AND AM KNOWINGLY AND VOLUNTARILY SIGNING ON OR AFTER THE SEPARATION DATE. Matthew Goldberg Date: 12

AND FOLDLAB AI LTD Exhibit 10.1 AMENDMENT AGREEMENT THIS AMENDMENT AGREEMENT (this “ Amendment ”) is dated for reference October 1, 2026 between Foldlab AI Ltd. (“ Seller ”) and iSpecimen Inc. (“ Buyer ”). Seller and Buyer are referred to together as the “ Parties ” and individually as a “ Party ”. WHEREAS the Parties entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement on or about September 4, 2026 (the “ Asset Purchase Agreement ”) for the purchase and sale of certain assets and related intellectual-property rights comprising the Disease-Associated Protein Discovery AI Agent and the Disease Trend Prediction and Monitoring AI Model as more particularly described therein, and the Parties now desire to confirm and amend certain terms thereof, as set out in this Amendment. NOW THEREFORE, the Parties agree as follows: 1. Unless otherwise defined herein, all capitalized terms used herein shall have the meaning ascribed to them in the Asset Purchase Agreement. 2. The Parties hereby confirm that the Execution Date of the Asset Purchase Agreement is September 4, 2026, and the text “[*], 2026” first appearing on page 1 thereof shall be replaced with the date “September 4, 2026”. 3. The Parties hereby confirm that the Stock Consideration will not be held in escrow under an escrow agreement, but will be issued and registered in restricted book-entry form in the name of Foldlab AI Ltd. Accordingly, the Parties hereby amend the Asset Purchase Agreement as follows: (a) in Section 2.2 the third sentence shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “The Stock Consideration is the number of whole shares of Buyer’s Common Stock equal to $2,500,000 divided by the VWAP, rounded down to the nearest whole share, issued at Closing and registered in restricted book-entry form in the name of Foldlab AI Ltd., subject to the five-year trading restriction, lock-up and no-leak-out restrictions in Section 2.4 and Exhibit F.” (b) in Subsection 2.2(b), the words “escrow hold” on the last line thereof shall be replaced with the words “share hold”; (c) in Subsection 2.2(c), the words “escrow hold” on the last line thereof shall be replaced with the words “share hold”; (d) Section 2.4 shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “ 2.4 Stock Consideration; Voting Rights. At Closing, Buyer shall issue and register the Stock Consideration in restricted book-entry form in the name of Foldlab AI Ltd., consisting of the number of whole shares of Common Stock equal to $2,500,000 divided by the VWAP and rounded down to the nearest whole share. Buyer may, in its discretion and in compliance with applicable Law, pay cash in lieu of any fractional-share amount or use another legally compliant method to account for it, without increasing the aggregate Purchase Price. The Payment Shares shall remain subject to a five-year trading restriction and lock-up beginning on the Closing Date, with no leak-out. The calculation and the restrictions applicable to the Stock Consideration shall be equitably adjusted for any stock split, reverse split, reclassification, recapitalization, merger, consolidation or similar event affecting the Common Stock. Upon the fifth anniversary of the Closing Date, Buyer shall deliver a written instruction to its transfer agent to remove the trading restriction and lock-up legend from the Payment Shares, other than any Payment Shares held under Section 12.4, and the Securities Act legends shall be removed when permitted under Rule 144 or another available exemption, on delivery of customary representations and, if required by the transfer agent, an opinion of counsel. Voting rights, dividend treatment and proxy mechanics shall be governed by the Voting Rights Agreement in Exhibit F.” (e) Subsection 4.5(c) shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “(c) When issued at Closing in accordance with this Agreement and applicable approvals, the Stock Consideration will be duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable, subject to the trading restrictions, lock-up, legend, no-leak-out and transfer restrictions in Exhibit F and the private-placement exemption selected by Buyer on advice of securities counsel. Buyer has authority to issue the Stock Consideration and to instruct its transfer agent to issue, register, legend, restrict and hold the Stock Consideration in accordance with this Agreement, applicable Law and the applicable transaction documents.” (f) in Section 7.4, the first sentence shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “The representations, warranties, covenants, indemnities and payment obligations of the Parties survive Closing for the periods stated in Section 11.12 and Section 12.1.” (g) Subsection 8.2(d) shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “(d) Closing Deliverables . Buyer has delivered or is ready, willing and able to deliver the $750,000 portion of the Cash Consideration at Closing, issue and register the Stock Consideration in restricted book-entry form, perform the testing and acceptance procedures described in Section 2.3 and Exhibit C, and deliver the Milestone Payments when due under Section 2.3, together with its officer’s certificate, the Voting Rights Agreement and all other documents required under Section 9.3.” (h) Subsection 9.3(d) shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “(d) Buyer shall issue and register the Stock Consideration under Section 2.4, using the share calculation specified in Section 2.4, subject to the five-year lock-up and no-leak-out restrictions;” (i) Subsection 9.3(e) shall be deleted and replaced with the words “Intentionally deleted”; (j) in Section 10.2, the words “escrow hold” on the last line thereof shall be replaced with the words “share hold”; (k) in Section 11.9, the words “the Escrow Agent or” shall be deleted; (l) in Section 11.12, the second sentence shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “Covenants survive according to their terms; milestone obligations survive until final acceptance or rejection and final resolution of any timely claim; and the trading restriction, lock-up, no-leak-out and voting obligations survive for five (5) years and through final resolution of any claim asserted during such period.” (m) in Section 11.13, on the second line thereof, the words “escrow release restrictions” shall be deleted; (n) in Section 11.14, on the third line thereof, “Escrowed Shares” shall be replaced with “Payment Shares” and on the fifth line thereof the words “escrow enforcement” shall be replaced with the words “share hold”; (o) in Section 11.15, the word “escrow” shall be deleted from the last sentence thereof; (p) in Section 11.17, on the third line thereof, the word “escrow” shall be replaced with the words “trading restrictions”; - 2 - (q) in Section 12.3, on the third line thereof, the words “or escrow release date” shall be deleted and on the last line thereof the words “relief, setoff or an escrow hold” shall be replaced with the words “relief, setoff or a share hold under Section 12.4”; (r) Section 12.4 shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “12.4 Setoff; Share Hold. Buyer may withhold, defer or set off any amount reasonably determined in good faith to be owed by Seller or an indemnifying party against any unpaid Milestone Payment, Transition Services fee or other amount payable by Buyer, after giving notice describing the basis and amount. Buyer may also, by written notice to Seller and its transfer agent, require that the trading restriction and lock-up legend remain on the number of Payment Shares reasonably related to any claim asserted before the fifth anniversary of the Closing Date until that claim is finally resolved, and, after a written agreement or final non-appealable determination establishing a covered Loss, cancel or require the return of Payment Shares having a value (based on the VWAP) equal to that Loss. Any cancellation or return of Payment Shares must be effected through that written agreement or final determination; no automatic forfeiture applies. No setoff or share hold may exceed the amount reasonably related to the asserted Loss, and a setoff or share hold does not waive any claim.” (s) in Section 12.6, on the second line thereof, the words “escrow enforcement” shall be replaced with the words “share hold”; (t) in Annex I – Definitions, (i) the definitions of “Escrow Agent” and “Escrow Agreement” shall be deleted; (ii) the definitions of “Stock Consideration” and “Escrowed Shares” shall be deleted and replaced with the following: “ Stock Consideration ” means the number of whole shares of Buyer’s Common Stock issued at Closing and registered in restricted book-entry form, equal to $2,500,000 divided by the VWAP and rounded down to the nearest whole share. Buyer may, in its discretion and in compliance with applicable Law, pay cash in lieu of any fractional-share amount or use another legally compliant method to account for it, without increasing the aggregate Purchase Price. “ Payment Shares ” means the Stock Consideration and refers in the Voting Rights Agreement to those same shares, together with all split shares and replacement securities attributable to them, all subject to the five-year trading restriction, lock-up, no-leak-out and voting-rights restrictions. (iii) in the definition of “Voting Rights Agreement”, “Escrowed Shares” shall be replaced with “Payment Shares”; (u) in Exhibit C, Schedule C-3 – Testing, Acceptance and Cure Procedure, the words “escrow hold” on the last line thereof shall be replaced with the words “share hold”; (v) Exhibit E – Form of Escrow Agreement shall be deleted and replaced with the words “Intentionally deleted”; and (w) Exhibit F – Form of Voting Rights Agreement shall be superseded by the Voting Rights Agreement in the form executed by the Parties at Closing, which reflects the absence of an escrow agreement and the issuance and registration of the Stock Consideration in restricted book-entry form. - 3 - 4. In Section 11.2 of the Asset Purchase Agreement, (a) the Seller’s address and contact person shall be deleted and replaced with: “Foldlab AI Ltd. 2500 – 700 West Georgia St. Vancouver, British Columbia V7Y 1B3 CANADA Attention: Jacob Shao, Director E-mail: jacob.z.shao@gmail.com” ; and (b) the Buyer’s address and contact person shall be deleted and replaced with: “iSpecimen Inc. 8 Cabot Road, Suite 1800 Woburn, MA 01801 USA Attention: Shahin Behroyan, Chief Executive Officer Email: sbehroyan@ispecimen.com” 5. Except as expressly modified by this Amendment, all of the terms, covenants, agreements, conditions and other provisions of the Asset Purchase Agreement, including all annexes, exhibits and attachments thereto, shall remain in full force and effect in accordance with their respective terms. 6. This Amendment and the legal relations among the Parties are governed by Delaware law, without regard to conflict-of-law rules. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Amendment as of the dates set out below. SELLER: Foldlab AI Ltd. BUYER: iSpecimen Inc.
